title: See, Think, Use: Diagnosing Perception and Reasoning Failures in VLMs
summary: We present See, Think, Use, a protocol that traces each answer of a vision-language model to perception, reasoning or the use of perception. The diagnosis shows a developer which stage to improve and directs test-time compute to the stage that fails. Benchmarks score the final answer, and an answer that rests on the image earns the same credit as a guess or a memorized prior. The protocol asks the model two extra questions per item and needs no access to its weights. A localization probe asks for a box around every instance and measures seeing, and a text-replacement probe answers from a description and measures thinking. Use is the rate at which the answer follows the model's own perception across counterfactual image pairs. The rate needs no answer labels, because the question and its prior are the same on both images. On two model families and six datasets the protocol shows that the knob that helps follows the task family. Answers follow the model's perception except on images that contradict a common prior, and asking the model to localize first repairs this failure when its boxes are right. Allocating compute by the measured stages comes close to the best uniform policy at lower cost and beats a random allocation of the same compute wherever a knob raises the short stage. We will release the code, the prompts and the per-question outputs.

AI.brief_summary: 提出「See、Think、Use」诊断协议：用定位探针测感知、文本替换探针测推理，并以反事实图像对上的无标签「Use」率衡量答案是否真正依据模型自身感知，进而把测试时算力导向失败阶段。
AI.relevance_reason: 与「答案是否使用视觉证据」及 THINK/LOOK 的收益成本直接相关：反事实对上的 Use 率可能成为视觉旁路与信息坍缩的度量，按阶段分配算力亦可供核查计算分配与停止策略。

title: VLMs Read Aloud: The Gap Between Recognizing and Using Visual Text
summary: Visual-text compression renders long contexts as images and is engineered around how much of the text a vision-language model (VLM) can recover. Yet recovered text is not usable text. VLMs can transcribe the text in an image word for word and still fail to answer from it; given back their own transcript, they answer nearly as well as from the original text. We call this difference the read-use gap. Recognizing and using visual text have different resolution requirements: Qwen3-VL-8B's recognition saturates at 15-pixel characters while use catches up only at 24 pixels, and scaling from 2B to 32B raises recognition without narrowing the gap. Putting the evidence into words closes it: thinking VLMs recite the evidence in their thinking, and their own transcript, written without seeing the question, recovers most of what thinking adds. In a preregistered held-out test, the gap ranks how much eight VLMs gain from their own words over pixels (Spearman $ρ$ = 0.86), which recognition rates do not. We propose ALOUD, which spends visual resolution on finding and recognizing evidence and language tokens on using it. Without keeping the source text, it doubles the accuracy of a frozen Qwen3-VL-8B on long documents compressed 5x and 10x: at 5x, from 27.7% to 54.8%, near the original text's 58.5%, with a context smaller than the compressed pages themselves. For less than the cost of reading the original text, it leads at equal budget every method that does without it, at every level, and beats AGAR and VERA, which paste the original text back; at 5x it also beats LensVLM-9B, which is trained and keeps the original text. Visual-text compression is limited not by how much text a model can recover, but by how much it can use.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出「read-use gap」，即 VLM 能逐字识别图像中的文本却无法据此作答；作者用识别与使用所需的分辨率差异、模型规模扩展及 preregistered 的 held-out 测试量化该差距，并据此提出 ALOUD：把视觉分辨率用于定位与识别证据，把语言 token 用于使用证据，在冻结的 Qwen3-VL-8B 上提升长文档压缩场景的准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接针对视觉证据是否真正被内部状态使用（而非仅被编码识别）这一核心问题，涉及信息坍缩、视觉旁路与「把证据转写为语言后即可用」的对比，其结论（瓶颈在使用而非恢复）可能直接影响视觉压缩与 latent 视觉推理的选题假设，值得优先核查。

title: Think Before You Locate: Clinical Chain-of-Though Supervision for Sequential Medical Image Grounding
summary: Clinicians rarely localize a finding from one image alone. They compare current and prior scans, follow structures across slices, and match regions across views or modalities. Yet vision-language models for sequential medical grounding usually learn only from bounding boxes. Boxes show where the target is, but they do not explain why that region in that image answers the question. We study whether explicit, image-grounded reasoning can improve localization, and which tasks benefit from it. We introduce method, whose core is MedChain, a corpus of 182,573 filtered rationales spanning eight sequential grounding tasks and ten imaging modalities. A medical VLM (FlemingVL-38B) first drafts a caption-like rationale, and a multimodal refiner (Qwen3.5-397B-A17B) then re-examines the images, question and annotated box to write a box-conditioned explanation with explicit cross-image reasoning. We fine-tune Qwen3.5 on these rationales with deliberative chain-of-thought supervision (dCoT-SFT). Across 4B, 9B, and 27B models, dCoT-SFT sets a new state of the art on MedSG-Bench. The 27B model reaches 77.24 mIoU and 85.20 Acc@0.5, improving over the strongest prior model by 4.69 and 5.49 points. In a paired comparison using fixed 4B checkpoints, dCoT-SFT improves over answer-only SFT by 3.56 mIoU (95% CI 3.13--4.00). The gains mainly come from change detection and object tracking, while performance drops on three appearance-matching tasks. Replacing a model's own rationale with a rationale from another task reduces mIoU by 12.2 points, showing that localization depends strongly on the reasoning context. Finally, adding GRPO with an IoU reward after dCoT-SFT gives only small and task-dependent gains, which we analyze through controlled multi-seed development experiments.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 MedChain（约18万条跨八类序贯定位任务的框条件医学 rationale），以 dCoT-SFT 微调 Qwen3.5 的 4B/9B/27B 模型，在 MedSG-Bench 上提升定位指标，并分析各任务收益差异及 GRPO 追加训练的有限效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「替换为其他任务的 rationale 后 mIoU 下降 12.2 点」与变化检测/跟踪增益、外观匹配任务的退化，可供核查显式推理内容是否真被定位使用，以及收益对任务类型的依赖；但监督与推理均为文本 CoT，非 latent 状态，可作对照而非同类方法。

title: MemU-Bench: Benchmarking GUI Agents on Long-Horizon User Interactions
summary: Existing Graphical User Interface (GUI) benchmarks predominantly rely on precise and stateless user instructions. In everyday usage, however, instructions are often \emph{vague and history-dependent}: users omit the exact details of their past operations because they no longer remember them, leaving the agent to recover the missing context from long and noisy interaction histories. To bridge this evaluation gap, we introduce \textbf{MemU-Bench}, a mobile benchmark of \textbf{118 vague tasks} grounded in 29 long-horizon user trajectories, where agents must distill raw interaction streams into memory and retrieve the missing context on demand, with task outcomes verified against serialized application databases. Alongside Success Rate, we incorporate Interaction Efficiency (IE) and Success weighted by Path Length (SPL) to expose agents that succeed by exhaustively searching across different applications rather than by \emph{genuinely recalling} the history. Evaluations show that without user history, state-of-the-art systems struggle under such ambiguity: the best-performing Gemini-3.1-Pro achieves an SPL of only 16.4\%, and end-to-end GUI agents fall below 5\%. To address this, we further propose \textbf{AppMem}, a training-free framework that distills user history into a \emph{structured, app-centric} memory bank, tracks interrupted intents across application switches, and selectively retrieves relevant memories via target-app inference. AppMem raises the SPL of GPT-5.5 from 15.7\% to 66.9\% (\textbf{+51.2\%}), outperforms a naive summary baseline by 9.3\%, and delivers consistent gains across evaluated backbones.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 MemU-Bench，用 118 个源自 29 条长程用户轨迹的模糊指令任务，评测 GUI agent 能否从冗长交互历史中提炼记忆并按需召回，并引入 IE、SPL 以区分「真正回忆」与穷举搜索；同时给出免训练的 AppMem 外部记忆框架。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 关注的多模态历史证据筛选、证据获取及推理成本度量直接相关；其 SPL/IE 可供核查 agent 是否真实使用记忆而非暴力搜索，但记忆是结构化外部存储而非内部 latent 状态，能否迁移到 latent 证据筛选仍需阅读判断。

title: SIEVE: Preserving Cross-Image Evidence via Depth-Aware Token Compression
comment: 19 pages, including supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/nitishshukla86/SIEVE
summary: Multi-image vision-language models (VLMs) incur substantial computation when processing long visual sequences. Compressing these sequences must preserve complementary evidence across images and keep tokens from different images separate. Global selection can underrepresent question-relevant images, and pruning in early decoder layers risks removing relevant content before sufficient multimodal processing, yet existing methods spend most of the budget on these early layers. We propose SIEVE, a training-free, single-pass framework that jointly allocates visual tokens across images and decoder depth. SIEVE first pools each image into a compact spatial grid to reduce early processing cost. It then progressively selects representatives using prompt attention under equal per-image quotas and aggregates unselected tokens into similar representatives from the same image. These operations keep every image represented and its tokens separate from other images, while refining the retained representations. A closed-form schedule sets retention counts to target a prescribed average token budget across decoder layers. Across four VLM backbones, SIEVE achieves the highest average at a 6.25% budget on five multi-image benchmarks and four single-image benchmarks, and the highest mean on two video benchmarks. On LLaVA-OneVision-7B, it outperforms the strongest baseline by 9.96 and 9.03 points at 6.25% and 12.5% budgets, and at 12.5% it exceeds the uncompressed model by 2.01 points with 6.6x fewer prefill FLOPs.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的单次视觉 token 压缩框架 SIEVE，按每图配额结合 prompt 注意力逐层选取代表 token，并把未选 token 聚合到同图代表上，用闭式调度在给定平均预算下跨图像与解码深度分配保留量。
AI.relevance_reason: 其“每图独立保留＋按深度分配预算”直接关涉多图互补视觉证据能否留在内部状态，可作为核查视觉旁路、信息坍缩与深度/位置对表示影响的压缩侧对照组，但该工作不涉及 latent 推理状态生成。

title: Spoofing the Latent State: Imperceptible Goal-Image Attacks Derail Planning in LeWorldModel
summary: Joint-embedding predictive architectures (JEPAs) have recently emerged as general-purpose visual world models for control. A prominent example is LeWorldModel (LeWM), which trains end-to-end from pixels using an isotropic Gaussian anti-collapse regularizer (SIGReg) and plans by minimizing the squared Euclidean distance between predicted and goal embeddings. In this work, we investigate the test-time robustness of this latent planning interface. Analyzing the learned metric on Push-T, we first find that task-relevant object state heavily dominates latent distance: shifting the block by a single pixel displaces the embedding $3\times$ further than an equivalent agent shift, and swapping the block pose alone accounts for $99\%$ of the distance between scene pairs. However, because this pose information is distributed across a curved, high-dimensional manifold rather than a fixed linear subspace, the encoder cannot be trivially edited post-hoc to isolate or redirect it. We next demonstrate that this geometry is highly vulnerable at test time. A white-box $\ell_\infty$ perturbation of just $ε{=}4/255$ applied to a single input frame causes the encoder to register the block at an arbitrary, attacker-chosen pose in $73$--$95\%$ of scenes without disturbing the encoded agent state. Perturbing either the goal image or the live camera observation drops Push-T planning success from $87\%$ to $32\%$, whereas uniform random noise at twice the magnitude has negligible impact. This vulnerability persists across all four standard LeWM benchmarks (Push-T, Two-Room, Reacher, and OGBench-Cube). At $ε{=}8/255$, the attack bridges $82$--$97\%$ of the squared latent distance to the target embedding in every environment, inducing planning degradation proportional to each task's reliance on the spoofed entity.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 LeWorldModel（JEPA 类视觉世界模型）latent 规划接口的测试期鲁棒性：先在 Push-T 上分析 latent 距离由哪些因素主导，再证明仅对单帧图像施加 ε=4/255 的白盒 ℓ∞ 扰动即可让编码器把物体登记为攻击者指定的位姿，并在四个基准上显著降低规划成功率。
AI.relevance_reason: 对 latent 距离的构成分析（物体位姿主导、分布于弯曲高维流形而无法线性编辑）以及「伪造 latent 即可改变目标匹配结果」的失败诊断，可供核查 LVR 中 latent 相似度作为目标或证据接口时实际编码的内容与视觉证据被误导的风险。

title: Do Multimodal Models Decide Consistently on Equivalent Optical Spectra?
comment: 20 pages, 4 figures, 11 tables. Code and data: https://github.com/zwang-devv/spectra-decision-audit
summary: A spectrum can be given to a model as a table in nanometers or as a plot in photon energy, and the decision should not depend on which one it sees. When the data needed for an answer are missing, the model should say so. We test representation invariance and abstention on measured optical spectra of silicon metasurfaces (MOCLIP) and gold nanoparticles, with labels computed from the data. Each spectrum is shown as four tables (nm, $μ$m, scientific notation, eV) and two plots (nm, eV), and partial spectra remove data inside or outside the queried range. We evaluate the decision models d3-nano and Jev 1.13, three GPT-6 Luna configurations and the Qwen3.5-2B base model. Changing only the representation moves accuracy by up to 41 percentage points within one model, mostly on photon-energy tables and plots. With the same evidence, asking in photon energy instead of wavelength helps some model-view pairs by 16-50 points and hurts others by up to 25. When the relevant extremum is removed, unadapted models rarely answer "undetermined". LoRA fine-tuning of d3-nano improves comparisons on the trained table formats, but much of its gain on unanswerable questions comes from a shortcut: it abstains whenever the input is truncated. Training with answerable truncations avoids the shortcut in all six seeds, with a 90-100 point gap between abstention after inside and outside cuts on held-out structures; with the same amount of extra original-task data, five of six seeds keep the shortcut. On gold spectra the two training sets perform similarly. Multimodal language models used for scientific decisions should be tested on equivalent representations and on missing evidence, not only on average accuracy. We release the tasks, per-response results and analysis code.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建光学光谱决策审计任务：同一光谱以四种表格（nm、μm、科学计数、eV）与两种图呈现，并删除查询范围内的关键数据制造缺证据情形，测试 d3-nano、Jev 1.13、三种 GPT-6 Luna 配置与 Qwen3.5-2B 的决策一致性与弃答，再用 LoRA 微调检验弃答是否依赖「输入被截断」这一捷径。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及多模态模型能否稳定使用视觉与表格证据、以及证据缺失时是否停止回答（对应 LOOK/STOP），其「仅改表征即偏移精度最多 41 点」和截断捷径诊断，可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节保留与弃答决策的基准与失败模式。

title: Selecting or Solving? What Best-of-N Verification Delivers in Video Reasoning
summary: Answering a complex question about a long video is a grounding problem: the answer turns on a few seconds of evidence, and vision-language models remain well below human accuracy at finding them. The standard way to spend extra test-time compute on this kind of video reasoning is best-of-N selection: sample several chain-of-thought answers from a fixed model, then let a second model re-watch the video and pick one. Such pipelines are reported by a single headline number, their margin over a majority vote. That number conflates two effects with opposite deployment consequences: the benefit the second model adds by selecting among candidates, and the benefit it would have supplied by solving the question itself. We separate them, measuring the Selection Increment (SI) -- selection accuracy minus the same verifier's accuracy with the candidates withheld -- alongside the margin over self-consistency, across five long-video benchmarks. The Selection Increment is largest for the weakest verifiers: a verifier that solves poorly on its own leaves the candidates the most room to help. Beating the majority vote follows the opposite profile: where the vote already sits near its ceiling no verifier we test improves on it; below that ceiling only the strongest do. On Video-Holmes, the two come apart on a single pool of candidates -- a weak verifier gains +19.3 points from the candidates yet lands 7.1 points below the vote, while the frontier verifier gains the least and beats the vote. The weakest verifier also shows a failure mode: on EgoSchema it picks by where an option sits in the list rather than by what the video shows. Read as a merit score, SI puts a verifier that fails to beat a majority vote at the top of its ranking; read as an audit, it says which of the two effects a headline number delivers. Code is available at https://github.com/facebookresearch/best-n-selection-video-reasoning.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究长视频推理中 best-of-N 验证的实际收益，将验证器的选择增益 SI 与其独立解题能力分开，并在五个基准上比较其相对多数投票的表现及失败模式。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接关联测试时额外计算、候选验证与视觉证据筛选；其揭示的弱验证器依赖选项位置、选择增益与解题能力错位，可能影响 LVR 中 latent 假设的验证与收益归因，值得近期核查。

title: Toward Counterfactual Learning for Selective Re-Examination in Agentic Visual Search
summary: Visual search over high-resolution images requires a vision-language model (VLM) not only to determine where to inspect, but also whether another observation is warranted before committing to an answer. Existing prompting, demonstrations, and outcome-based reinforcement learning can encourage re-examination, yet do not directly supervise whether it is beneficial at a particular search state. We introduce ReSee, a benchmark of re-examination decisions comprising 3,227 visual-search trajectories and 8,827 explicit commit-or-re-examine decisions, with counterfactual adjudication that distinguishes states where additional inspection is warranted from those where commitment is preferable. Building on this formulation, we propose CARE (Counterfactual Advantage for Re-Examination), a decision-level reinforcement learning method that compares paired continuations under commit and re-examine verdicts from the same search state. Their cost-aware return difference estimates the counterfactual value of an additional observation and is assigned only to the corresponding verdict tokens, providing localized credit for whether search should continue. Experiments expose limited re-examination selectivity in existing VLMs and show that CARE significantly improves accuracy and decision selectivity over GRPO across two backbones, with higher accuracy and fewer visual requests on six unseen OOD benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 ReSee 基准，用 3,227 条视觉搜索轨迹和 8,827 个显式「提交或再检查」决策，并以反事实裁决区分「值得再看一次」与「应直接作答」的搜索状态；在此基础上提出 CARE，通过比较同一状态下 commit 与 re-examine 两条配对续写的成本感知回报差，估计额外观察的反事实价值，并将该优势只分配给对应决策 token，实现局部化信用分配。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应 LOOK/STOP 的收益—成本判定与停止决策，其「反事实价值估计＋决策级局部信用分配＋选择性指标」可供核查是否优于结果型 RL，以及成本项是否真能约束无效重复观察。

title: StreamClarify: Proactive Clarification for Grounded Streaming Video Question Answering
summary: Streaming video question answering (QA) requires real-time reasoning over continuous video streams under strict latency and active-context budgets. Current streaming vision-language models (VLMs) often give confident yet ungrounded answers when queries are ambiguous or have false premises, or when relevant visual evidence is no longer in the active context. Proactive clarification can help, but must satisfy the same latency and memory constraints. We present StreamClarify, a training-free framework for grounded streaming QA that combines a pre-answer uncertainty check with hierarchical memory. The check uses the entropy of a binary pre-answer judgment as a lightweight uncertainty score to decide whether to answer directly or request clarification. To support re-answering, a temporal-pyramid KV cache maintains a bounded active visual context, while a CPU-side semantic retrieval archive provides access to historical frames. We further construct StreamClarify-QA, a diagnostic benchmark of 1,837 QA pairs from StreamBench and OVO-Bench, spanning standard, referential ambiguity, and unanswerable scenarios. Across three VLM backbones, StreamClarify improves Macro accuracy by up to 8.2 points over backbone-matched baselines. At comparable trigger rates, entropy-based selection achieves more than 18 points higher precision than random selection in identifying initially incorrect answers. Under oracle user guidance, clarification improves Macro accuracy by up to 3.5 points. We also report a controlled, oracle-assisted Qwen3-VL simulation on Ambiguous QA with generated questions and referent-only user replies, where the entropy-gated condition improves accuracy by 8.3 points.

AI.brief_summary: 提出免训练的流式视频问答框架：用二分类预答判断的熵作为不确定性分数，决定直接回答还是主动澄清，并结合时序金字塔 KV cache 与 CPU 端语义检索档案支持重答，同时构建含歧义和不可回答场景的诊断基准。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及视觉证据是否仍在活跃上下文中、何时停止回答并请求澄清，以及有界记忆与历史检索的成本；可供核查不确定性门控对 STOP 决策精度和证据筛选的影响，但未生成 latent 推理状态。

title: FOCUS: Closed-Loop Attention Feedback for Efficient Vision-Language Understanding
summary: Processing every video frame through Vision-Language Models (VLMs) adds significant inference cost and limits their ability to comprehend real-time video. Existing approaches either sub-sample frames uniformly, ignoring content and missing important events, or prune visual tokens inside the VLM to cut per-call cost while still invoking the model on every sampled frame. We introduce FOCUS, a training-free three-layer framework that reduces the number of invocations and steers each one towards what matters. Temporal gating measures inter-frame dissimilarity in the patch-embedding space of a smaller VLM from the same family, triggering burst captures only when the scene changes in a semantically meaningful way. Patch-level dissimilarity is then accumulated across the burst and fused with a top-down attention prior into a spatial focus map that encodes where motion and semantic relevance coincide. That map calibrates the VLM's value cache during generation, progressively amplifying vision tokens in task-relevant regions and attenuating off-target ones, without removing any token from the context. The loop closes after each response: text-to-vision cross-attention is extracted from the decoder and fed back as the prior for the next burst, letting the system converge on semantically important regions over successive observations. We evaluate FOCUS on the 500-video EgoSchema subset in streaming mode, with a single Qwen3-VL-8B backbone shared by every method. It reaches 74.8% accuracy using 25.4 VLM calls per clip, against 74.6% with 55 calls for uniform sampling and 74.2% with 55 calls for BOLT. On egocentric video captioning across four domains, it matches the best baseline's quality while issuing 57% fewer VLM invocations than uniform sampling.

AI.brief_summary: FOCUS 提出免训练的三层框架：用小 VLM 的 patch 嵌入差异做时间门控决定何时采集，将 burst 内 patch 差异与自上而下注意力先验融合为空间关注图，并据此校正生成时的 value cache，再把解码器的文本-视觉跨注意力回传为下一轮先验，以减少 VLM 调用并聚焦任务相关区域。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「何时看、看哪里」的门控与闭环注意力反馈直接关联 LVR 的视觉证据筛选及 LOOK 侧收益成本；不删除 token 而靠 value cache 调制视觉状态，可供核查注意力与缓存结构对证据保留和 latent 相似度的影响。

title: Label-Free Localization and Test-Time Suppression of CLIP's Typographic Circuits
summary: CLIP-based Vision-Language Models have become cornerstones of modern multimodal systems. The cross-modal contrastive objective equips the CLIP vision encoder to both see objects and read text. These two abilities induce an entanglement between the encoding of lexical and semantic shapes, creating a distinctive vulnerability to typographic attacks, in which rendered text overrides an image's semantic content with its literal meaning. The black-box nature of these encoders has prevented a mechanistic interpretation of such entanglement. We introduce a head-decomposed Sparse Dictionary Learning (SDL) architecture that, by design, decomposes individual attention heads into interpretable, head-specific latents. Based on this inductive disentanglement, we re-purpose Clarity Score and propose normalized Text Attribution Score, which are both label-free, to identify attention heads that carry typographic information. As a causal validation of successful circuit separation, we perform a mechanistic intervention that reweighs attention away from the patch tokens in the identified lexical heads at test-time. Experiments show that the intervention effectively recovers object classification under typographic attack and, across five CLIP variants and four typographic benchmarks, achieves up to 46.9% improvement while incurring up to 1% accuracy loss in general image perception, outperforming prior supervised and training-free methods. Expanding on the mechanistic intervention, we propose a test-time adaptive attention head routing to further reduce the impact on performance at matched robustness, pushing beyond the Pareto frontier of current robustness-perception tradeoff.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出按注意力头分解的稀疏字典学习结构，用无标签的 Clarity Score 与归一化 Text Attribution Score 定位 CLIP 中承载排版文字信息的注意力头，并通过测试时重加权及自适应头路由抑制排版攻击。

title: MMCoT$^3$: Empowering 3D Scene Understanding with 3D-Text Interleaved Multi-Modal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 4 tables. Accepted to ACM Multimedia 2026
summary: Understanding and reasoning over 3D scenes from point clouds is essential for a broad range of AI applications. Recent 3D large language models have shown promising results, yet they still face two fundamental limitations: (i) insufficient capability for grounded multi-step reasoning in complex 3D scenes, and (ii) a text-centric inference paradigm that lacks effective interaction between textual reasoning and visual evidence. As a result, these models often fail to verify intermediate inferences, disambiguate similar object instances, and avoid hallucinations. To address these limitations, we propose MMCoT$^3$, the first 3D-Text Interleaved Chain-of-Thought (CoT) framework for 3D scene understanding. The core idea is to explicitly interleave textual reasoning with task-relevant 3D evidence, enabling the model to consult scene observations throughout the reasoning process. In addition, since a textual mention in 3D scenes may correspond to multiple candidate objects, naive object-mention alignment can inject incorrect evidence and mislead subsequent reasoning. To mitigate this multi-instance ambiguity, we design an ambiguity-aware evidence aggregation mechanism that uses query-guided cross-attention to fuse candidate object tokens and inject both evidence and ambiguity cues into the reasoning process. To better equip the model with multi-step reasoning capability, we further develop PointCoT, a large-scale 3D-specific CoT instruction tuning dataset with approximately 176.2K instances spanning captioning, question answering, dialogue, and planning tasks. Extensive experiments on six benchmarks show that our method consistently improves performance and achieves state-of-the-art results, validating the effectiveness of our proposed ambiguity-aware 3D-text interleaved reasoning for 3D scene understanding.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 MMCoT$^3$，一个将文本推理步骤与任务相关 3D 证据显式交错的点云场景 CoT 框架，用 query-guided cross-attention 聚合多候选物体 token 并注入歧义线索，同时构建约 176.2K 实例的 3D CoT 指令微调数据集 PointCoT。

title: When Does Latent Prediction Error Support Physical Surprise Claims in Video World Models?
comment: 28 pages, 12 figures, 25 tables. Accepted at the World Models in Physical AI Workshop, NeurIPS 2026
summary: Prediction errors from video world models are often treated as physical surprise, but they can also reflect appearance, static content, motion, or ordinary prediction difficulty. We present an evaluation framework that separates what frozen representations contain, how they organize appearance and physical differences, and what changes a model's own prediction error. On IntPhys2, a benchmark of physically possible and impossible events, we compare representations from latent prediction, masked pixel reconstruction, and simple visual statistics. Appearance remains easy to decode, while V-JEPA2 exposes modest information about whether events are possible or impossible. Looking at the latent geometry, appearance changes become smaller compared with differences between videos, their directions line up more consistently across scenes, and their overlap with physical changes decreases in deeper layers. Across action-conditioned models, incorrect actions raise prediction error, while appearance changes also produce substantial responses. In Physion++ video clips, repeating a single frame can produce higher error than the original clip, while changing color throughout the clip can lower it. Using Kubric, a simulation and rendering framework, we find that impossible events can produce lower error than possible events. A fixed error threshold also incorrectly flags many possible events as impossible. A model can therefore represent physical information and respond to incorrect actions without its native prediction error reliably measuring physical surprise.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出评估框架，区分冻结视频世界模型表示中包含什么、外观与物理差异在潜空间几何中如何组织，以及模型预测误差如何响应动作错误、外观变化与物理不可能事件，并在 IntPhys2、Physion++ 和 Kubric 上检验「预测误差即物理惊讶」这一假设。
AI.relevance_reason: 其关于潜表示内容、外观与物理因素解耦及误差信号有效性的诊断，直接关联 LVR 中「latent 是否保留任务必要视觉信息」与「误差或证据信号能否支撑停止与计算分配」的评价问题，可供核查。

title: SurgQ-VLM: Question-Conditioned Dual-Stream Compression and Answer-Type-Aware Reinforcement for Surgical Video Question Answering
comment: Accepted to WACV 2027 (Applications track). 16 pages: 8-page main paper, references, and supplementary material. Code: https://github.com/DhruvMakwana/SurgQ-VLM ; Weights: https://huggingface.co/dhruvmakwana/SurgQ-VLM-7B
summary: Reasoning about surgical video -- which phase is underway, which instruments act, and when events occur -- underpins operative documentation, workflow analysis, and skill assessment. Yet surgical visual question answering is still largely built on single frames and closed labels that cannot express a duration, an ordering, or a count, and the video models that lift the frame limit typically compress every clip the same way regardless of the question, discarding the temporal evidence the answer needs. Worse, the answers are structurally heterogeneous, spanning five incompatible structures -- binary, classification, multi-label, counting, and sentence-temporal -- that no single training signal scores uniformly well. We propose SurgQ-VLM, a two-stage model for surgical video question answering. Stage 1 trains a question-conditioned dual-stream (slow/fast) compressor for a LoRA-adapted Qwen2.5-VL-7B: cross-attention conditions both streams on the question, and each clip's visual tokens shrink 49x from the raw ViT patches (11x vs. post-merge backbone tokens). Stage 2 post-trains with GRPO under an answer-type-aware reward that scores each question on the metric matching its answer structure (micro-F1 for label sets, normalised error for counts, a content-timing blend for temporal windows). On a sealed 21,840-question test split over Cholec80 and CholecT50, SurgQ-VLM reaches 0.779 keyword accuracy and a 10x BLEU-4 gain over zero-shot; GRPO adds 2.5 pp K-Acc (2.0 pp attributable to the answer-type-aware reward), concentrated in the structurally hard types, with answer format unchanged (ROUGE-L). Code is available at https://github.com/DhruvMakwana/SurgQ-VLM.

AI.brief_summary: SurgQ-VLM 面向手术视频问答：用问题条件的慢/快双流交叉注意力把视觉 token 压缩约 49 倍，再以按答案类型定制奖励的 GRPO 后训练，统一处理二分类、多标签、计数与时序答案。

title: NAS-PO: Native Attention-Strategy Policy Optimization for Vision-Language Models
summary: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) has become an effective post-training paradigm for vision-language models (VLMs). Standard RLVR, however, assigns identical outcome-derived credit to all generated tokens regardless of their perceptual relevance. Recent perception-aware methods estimate visual reliance through image perturbation or masking. These indirect proxies require perturbation branches, while corruption sensitivity does not necessarily identify the visual evidence used for reasoning. We instead shape model perception through native attention, an intrinsic model signal. Rather than treating attention as a post-hoc explanation, we formulate it as a reward-anchored, token-aligned routing signal that encourages attention patterns supporting visually grounded reasoning. To this end, we propose NAS-PO, a Native Attention-Strategy Policy Optimization framework. NAS-PO analyzes native attention with a visual mass policy that quantifies visual allocation and a conditional visual policy that captures spatial routing over visual tokens, making the optimization well-posed. Based on this, Native Attention-Strategy Advantage Shaping (NAS-AS) draws on the visual-mass policy to redistribute signed policy-gradient credit for visually engaged rollouts. The Adaptive Attention-Coupled (AAC) loss then aligns the visual-mass policy on all response tokens and the conditional visual policy on visually active ones, consolidating the visual-routing patterns that drive successful trajectories. Experiments demonstrate that NAS-PO substantially surpasses leading RL-tuned VLMs across 7 out-of-domain reasoning and perception benchmarks, with its effectiveness consistently validated across 8B and 32B. Visual-Routing Sensitivity (VRS) analysis further indicates that the optimized attention prioritizes visually load-bearing regions.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 NAS-PO，在 VLM 的 RLVR 后训练中以原生注意力作为路由信号，通过视觉质量策略与条件视觉策略重分配 token 级策略梯度 credit，并加入注意力耦合损失，在 7 个域外推理与感知基准上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接触及 LVR 关心的视觉证据使用与贡献分配：其以原生注意力替代扰动代理来筛选视觉承载区域，可供核查 token 级 credit 与「LOOK」证据定位；但未生成或分析 latent 推理状态。

title: Reconstruction as Spatial Evaluation: Diagnosing Cross-View Spatial Intelligence in Large Vision-Language Models
summary: The spatial intelligence of large vision-language models (LVLMs) requires the ability to combine local visual observations into a geometrically consistent representation of the physical world. Many static benchmarks assess isolated spatial judgments, such as relative direction or distance, while interactive embodied evaluations combine perception with exploration, planning, control, and simulator-specific execution. To bridge this gap, we introduce RECONSPATIAL, a benchmark centered on multi-view 3D scene reconstruction across indoor, tabletop, and outdoor environments. Given real multi-view images and target-object queries, LVLMs are required to jointly predict oriented 3D bounding boxes in a shared, camera-anchored metric coordinate frame. Reconstructions are evaluated along two complementary axes: Structure for relative layout and Metric for physical scale and camera-anchored placement. Nine atomic spatial QA tasks, grouped into Geometric Perception and Spatial Relations, probe spatial capabilities involved in joint reconstruction. Offline navigation extends evaluation to path planning. Evaluation of 18 frontier LVLMs reveals a consistent gap between relative scene structure and metric reconstruction; even GPT-6-Astra scores 81.4% on Structure but only 58.7% on Metric. Tracing this gap, diagnostic analyses link atomic spatial capabilities to reconstruction quality and show that relational consistency alone does not ensure metric accuracy. Experiments with 3D map injection further separate scene construction from path planning, revealing how these geometric errors limit navigation success. Finally, spatial fine-tuning yields broad transfer across both spatial and general vision-language benchmarks.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 RECONSPATIAL 基准，用室内、桌面与室外真实多视图图像要求 LVLM 在统一相机坐标系中联合预测带朝向的 3D 包围盒，并按结构与度量两轴评价 18 个前沿模型，辅以原子空间问答、离线导航诊断与空间微调实验。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准直接诊断多视图几何与度量尺度信息能否被模型整合为一致的空间表示，其「结构尚可但度量不足」的发现可供核查 LVR 中视觉细节保留与信息坍缩问题，也可作为潜在空间状态几何评价的参照。

title: Learning to Look: A Foundation for Visual Understanding
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) suffer from visual hallucination, such as saying an object that is not present in an image. We ask a more fundamental question: whether a VLM is even aware of where it is looking before understanding the semantic meaning in the image. We formulate this question as a LOOK task: identifying which parts of its visual input were available to the model. We construct the task in a self-supervised way without manually labeling the available region to the model. Our experiments show that existing VLMs fail to localize the visible region. We further show that fine-tuning VLMs on the proposed LOOK task improves a model's awareness of visual input.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出自监督的 LOOK 任务，要求 VLM 识别其视觉输入中哪些区域实际可见，并发现现有模型难以定位可见区域，而针对该任务微调可提升模型对视觉输入的感知。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作直接诊断 VLM 对「自己看到了什么」的内部可用性，与视觉证据筛选、位置/可见性状态表示及视觉幻觉相关，可供核查 LOOK 能力是否影响 latent 推理中的证据使用与停止决策。

title: Scene-Adaptive Readout and Decoding in Diffusion Driving VLAs
summary: Diffusion driving vision-language-action models repeatedly execute the backbone at every denoising stage, incurring substantial inference cost, while it remains unclear whether all scenes require the same decoding computation. To distinguish when a trajectory becomes readable from how much further refinement it requires, we analyze trajectory readout across network depth and decoding progress. We identify a depth-decoding dissociation in which late-layer representations already support useful trajectory readout after the first forward sweep, whereas early-layer representations benefit more from continued decoding. We further find that both the preferred readout layer and decoding depth vary across scenes. Based on these observations, we propose a scene-adaptive readout and decoding framework. A scene-conditioned readout MoE adaptively weights and combines trajectory predictions from layer-specific late-layer representations after a single backbone sweep, while an adaptive decoding policy applies additional native refinement only when required by the scene. We evaluate our framework on two diffusion driving VLAs across the Waymo E2E and nuScenes benchmarks. Our method improves validation RFS by up to 0.56 while also improving test performance, and achieves an end-to-end speedup of up to $6.0\times$ on Waymo E2E, while consistently reducing trajectory error on nuScenes. These results demonstrate that scene-level readout and decoding allocation improves planning quality while avoiding unnecessary decoding. Our code is available at https://github.com/sjyu001/SARD

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析 diffusion driving VLA 中轨迹读出随网络深度与去噪进度的变化，发现深层表示在首次前向即可支持有效读出、而偏好读出层与解码深度随场景而异，据此提出场景条件的读出 MoE 与自适应解码策略，在 Waymo E2E 与 nuScenes 上提升规划指标并显著加速。

title: Blueprint2CAD: Benchmarking Foundation Models on Engineering Drawing-to-CAD Render Correspondence
summary: Engineering drawings specify mechanical parts through orthographic projections. Recognizing which part a drawing depicts underlies part search, design reuse, and digitization, yet no public benchmark measures whether vision models can do it. We introduce Blueprint2CAD, a benchmark for drawing-to-render correspondence: given an orthographic line drawing and a shaded render, usually from another viewpoint, decide whether they show the same part. Its data layer, BlueCAD-30K, applies an open drafting pipeline to 29,925 Zero-to-CAD models, adding view-aligned renders, clean and dimensioned drawings from six viewpoints, and surface-type metadata. Frozen encoders retrieve the matching part from a 10,000-model gallery with up to 65% Recall@1 when viewpoints are known but 43% when they are not, and the four encoders we test lie within six points of each other: viewpoint, not backbone, is the bottleneck. Six zero-shot vision-language models reach only 0.52-0.67 verification accuracy, with model-specific Yes/No biases that chain-of-thought shifts but does not remove; a quick LoRA fine-tuning on in-domain pairs improves verification accuracy by a few points but sharpens these biases and leaves the viewpoint failure intact.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 Blueprint2CAD 基准，用工程三视图线图与另一视角的着色渲染判断是否同一零件，并系统评测冻结编码器检索与零样本、LoRA 微调 VLM 的验证表现。
AI.relevance_reason: 其诊断显示瓶颈在视角而非骨干，且 CoT 只移动不消除 Yes/No 偏置，可为核查 VLM 几何与视角证据是否真正进入内部状态、以及推理链长度与证据筛选的收益提供对照。

title: GeoGuesser Bench: Benchmarking Vision-Language Agents on Interactive Geolocation
summary: Vision-language model (VLM) agents that act in the open world need two abilities: world knowledge to interpret what they see, and exploration to find what they cannot yet see. We study how agents combine the two through interactive visual geolocation. GeoGuesser Bench contains 282 tasks in an offline Street View environment where agents rotate, zoom, and move between real panoramas. Its three task types shift the balance from knowledge to exploration: agents (1) report the coordinates of their starting location, (2) name the enclosing street, city, state, or country, or (3) find, read, and count nearby objects. The coordinate tasks in (1) also include 42 real GeoGuessr World Championship rounds, whose expert guesses provide a human reference. We evaluate 23 VLMs: the best accuracy is 62.5% on place naming and 35.0% on object finding, and the best agent averages 4352.4 GeoGuessr points on the championship rounds, against 4770.3 for the better expert in each round. Beyond these headline numbers, world knowledge and exploration are only weakly correlated across models: agents that localize well do not necessarily explore well. To understand where agents fail, we categorize their errors into vision, navigation, and tool-use failures. Further ablations show that the strongest agents, such as Claude Opus 4.8, still perform well with limited views, while weaker agents degrade; customizing the environment thus adjusts task difficulty. The environment's verifiable rewards and restorable state also support training, and our Planner-Worker-Compressor harness cuts planner tokens by 57-61% by compacting the interaction history. We hope GeoGuesser Bench and its environment serve as a high-quality foundation for simulating real-world exploration at scale.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 GeoGuesser Bench：282 个离线 Street View 交互定位任务，含坐标、地名与目标查找三类，评测 23 个 VLM 智能体的探索与世界知识结合能力，并对视觉、导航与工具使用错误归类，另提出 Planner-Worker-Compressor 框架压缩交互历史。
AI.relevance_reason: 它测量多轮视觉证据获取中「继续看还是作答」的取舍，并发现定位能力与探索能力弱相关，可供核查 LOOK/STOP 的收益成本与能力分离；受限视角 ablation 与历史压缩机制也可能与上下文/缓存对推理的影响相关。

title: Beyond Answers, Traces, and Efficiency: Evidence for Adaptive Reasoning
summary: Current AI systems are evaluated as reasoners through final-answer accuracy, reasoning traces, process supervision, and computational or human-relative efficiency. Yet these measures do not establish whether reasoning adapts when tasks or evidence change. We distinguish across-task adaptivity, where acquired abstractions transfer or recombine across novel problems, fromwithin-task adaptivity, where hypotheses and actions are revised in response to new observations, feedback, or counterexamples. Using ARC-AGI as a diagnostic case study rather than an alignment benchmark, we examine what existing measures leave unresolved when test-time search, sampling, or adaptation affects performance. We propose intervention-oriented evaluation that tests abstraction transfer and hypothesis revision under controlled changes to tasks and evidence, with explicit reporting of test-time procedures and budgets. This perspective supports evaluating systems for robustness, responsiveness to corrective feedback, and auditability under changing conditions.

AI.brief_summary: 该文是一篇评估视角论文，以ARC-AGI为诊断案例，区分跨任务自适应性（抽象迁移与重组）与任务内自适应性（依据新观察、反馈或反例修正假设），并提出干预式评估：在受控改变任务与证据的条件下检验抽象迁移和假设修正，同时显式报告测试时搜索、采样与预算。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接呼应LVR关注的可变计算、证据获取与停止决策的评价问题，其「显式报告测试时流程与预算」及干预式设计可供核查能否用于判断latent状态是否真正随视觉证据更新、以及长度/预算泛化结论是否被搜索掩盖。

title: Trace4D: Grounded Spatiotemporal Reasoning via 4D State Sequences
summary: Understanding how objects and their spatial relationships evolve in 3D space over time remains challenging for vision-language models (VLMs), particularly under changing viewpoints. Recent approaches incorporate geometric information into reasoning, but explicit supervision for temporally ordered 4D state evolution and its use as intermediate evidence remains limited. We introduce \textbf{Trace4D}, which trains VLMs to predict 4D state sequences and reason over their inter-timestep changes alongside temporal visual observations. Its 4D-grounded chain-of-thought (CoT) explicitly represents 4D states, analyzes temporal visual context, and connects both as evidence for the answer. We construct Trace4D-Train from in-the-wild videos with 600K 4D perception examples and approximately 70K grounded QA examples, and train with joint supervised fine-tuning followed by geometry-aware GRPO. At inference, Trace4D predicts 4D states and reasoning directly from video without reference annotations or an external geometric model. Experiments on Trace4D-Bench and VLM4D show improved QA accuracy over the base VLMs and benefits from reasoning over 4D state changes and temporal visual observations.

AI.brief_summary: Trace4D 训练 VLM 从视频直接预测 4D 状态序列，并与时间视觉观察一起构成 4D-grounded 链式推理，将状态及其跨时间步变化作为答案证据；构建 60 万 4D 感知与约 7 万 grounded QA 数据，采用监督微调加几何感知 GRPO，在 Trace4D-Bench 与 VLM4D 上提升问答准确率。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「显式状态序列作为中间证据」与 LVR 中内部状态是否保留几何/时序必要信息、答案是否真正使用该证据直接相关，可供核查显式 4D 状态与 latent 状态在证据筛选和变化建模上的异同。

title: Lookahead Prediction-Guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing for Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning
summary: Interleaved multimodal chain-of-thought reasoning improves the visual reasoning capabilities of multimodal large language models by dynamically incorporating visual evidence during reasoning. However, existing methods primarily select evidence from historical context. When the reasoning focus shifts, history-guided evidence may remain focused on prior regions and fail to cover the visual information required by the next step. We refer to this lag between visual evidence and subsequent reasoning demands as Temporal Evidence Myopia. To address this issue, we propose Lookahead Prediction-guided Adaptive Visual Refocusing (LPAVR), a training-free test-time framework. LPAVR transforms Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) from a decoding acceleration mechanism into a lookahead signal for anticipating upcoming reasoning intent. During MTP decoding, the draft head generates multiple future tokens, while the target model verifies them in parallel and retains the longest prefix consistent with its decoding trajectory. This target-verified prefix contains near-future semantics, which LPAVR uses to construct lookahead-guided visual evidence and assess whether history-guided evidence covers the indicated regions. If the coverage is sufficient, the history-guided evidence is retained; otherwise, LPAVR switches to the lookahead-guided evidence. This better aligns the visual context with upcoming reasoning and improves consistency between draft predictions and target-model decoding. Experiments on multiple multimodal reasoning benchmarks show that LPAVR improves both reasoning accuracy and the acceptance rates of MTP speculative tokens, jointly enhancing visual reasoning and speculative decoding efficiency.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出免训练的测试时框架 LPAVR，利用 MTP 草稿 token 经目标模型验证后的前缀作为前瞻信号，预测下一步推理意图，并在历史证据覆盖不足时切换到前瞻引导的视觉证据；在多模态推理基准上同时评估准确率与投机解码接受率。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接涉及交错多模态推理中的视觉证据筛选与重新聚焦时机，其「前瞻意图＋覆盖判断」可供核查 LOOK 决策及证据获取成本；但方法作用于显式视觉上下文，未涉及 latent 状态生成。

title: VizDAGuide: Misleading Chart Question Answering in Compact Vision Language Models via DAG-Structured Supervision
summary: Misleading charts can lead vision-language models to conclusions that conflict with underlying data. Existing work focuses on inference-time strategies, while training-time supervision remains less explored. We present VizDAGuide, a DAG-structured supervision method for misleading-chart question answering. The method represents intermediate reasoning states and their dependencies as a directed acyclic graph, assigns supervision weights according to their roles, and serializes the graph into a unified training target for open-ended and multiple-choice QA with single-pass inference. Experiments on two benchmarks across Qwen3-VL and InternVL3.5 models show improvements over a content- and weight-matched Linear CoT-SFT baseline on both answer formats. Process-level evaluation shows gains in grounding and operation execution, while ablations indicate that dependency structure and weighted supervision are most effective when combined. These results support DAG-structured weighted supervision for misleading-chart question answering.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究误导性图表问答中紧凑 VLM 的训练期监督，提出 VizDAGuide：把中间推理状态及其依赖关系表示为有向无环图，按各状态的角色分配监督权重，并将图序列化为统一训练目标，使开放式与多选 QA 都能单次前向推理。
AI.relevance_reason: 直接对应「轨迹训练、贡献分配与监督」这条线：DAG 依赖结构与加权监督可供核查逐步 credit assignment 及 grounding 是否真正被使用；但它是显式结构化 CoT 监督而非 latent 状态生成，其过程评测口径与对信息坍缩的启示尚待读原文确认。

title: MIRA: Reinforcing Multimodal Reasoning via Deceptive Contextual Augmentation
summary: While Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) has significantly advanced multimodal reasoning, existing frameworks suffer from a critical "perception-reasoning gap." Due to an over-reliance on seemingly relevant visual tokens, even minor perceptual perturbations can propagate through the reasoning process, leading to compounding hallucinations. To address this issue, we propose MIRA, a training framework that improves robustness to erroneous visual contexts while enhancing logical reasoning ability. By injecting filtered, deceptive visual contexts during training, we construct challenging "hard traps" that stress-test the model's robustness to misleading information. Furthermore, we introduce a group-wise reflection-triggering mechanism that enables the model to autonomously detect and rectify inconsistencies between visual cues and logical constraints, which is ultimately internalized as an intrinsic policy behavior. Importantly, MIRA does not rely on human annotations. Experimental results across multiple reasoning and perception benchmarks show that MIRA yields an average 7% improvement on in-domain benchmarks, with consistent improvements on vision-centric benchmarks. These findings highlight that active error recovery is essential for robust multimodal reasoning. Comprehensive ablation studies and analyses further provide insights into why MIRA is effective.

AI.brief_summary: MIRA 提出一种多模态推理训练框架，在训练中注入经过筛选的欺骗性视觉上下文以构造「硬陷阱」，并引入组内反思触发机制，使模型自主发现并纠正视觉线索与逻辑约束之间的矛盾。

title: DR Pixel: Page-Native Deep Research with Vision-Language Models
summary: Complex documents such as scientific papers contain rich information in tables, figures, and equations; however, existing deep research (DR) agents typically reduce papers to OCR-extracted text. We instead ask whether vision-language models (VLMs) can enable page-native deep research: directly retrieving and reasoning over rendered document page images. We introduce DR Pixel, the first open-source end-to-end multimodal DR agent that uses rendered page images as its sole retrieval and reasoning unit, operating over a corpus of 1.06M pages. To evaluate this setting, we construct DRPixelBench, a benchmark on scientific papers requiring reasoning over text, figures, tables, and equations. Surprisingly, page-native DR already works well without training, outperforming OCR-based baselines across state-of-the-art models like GPT-5.4, Gemini-3.5-Flash, and Qwen3.6-27B, while requiring fewer tool calls. We next turn to DR training. A key challenge is that teacher trajectories for agentic supervised finetuning are noisy, mixing critical reasoning and action steps with redundant or failed attempts. To address this, we introduce counterfactual credit reweighting, a fine-grained credit assignment method that weights individual reasoning and action steps by their counterfactual contribution to the final answer. Our training improves retrieval recall by about 15 points and final accuracy by over 10 points on DRPixelBench, and likewise outperforms the untrained baseline on four existing benchmarks. On out-of-distribution ViDoRe-V3, DR Pixel comes within 1.8 points of an oracle that is given the gold pages directly. Our results suggest that the conventional OCR-then-retrieve pipeline is not only unnecessary but suboptimal: directly retrieving and reasoning over visual document pages makes complex DR both more effective and more efficient.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 DR Pixel，以渲染页面图像作为唯一检索与推理单元构建端到端多模态深度研究智能体，并构建 DRPixelBench，同时用反事实贡献重加权训练教师轨迹。

title: Same Outputs, Different Scores: Auditing the Unchecked Graders of Multimodal LLM Benchmarks
comment: Accepted at WACV 2027 (Evaluations and Datasets Track). Code and data: https://github.com/ahmadhasan2k8/grader-audit
summary: Every multimodal-LLM multiple-choice benchmark ends with a scoring rule that converts a model's response, often free-form text rather than a clean option letter, into a right/wrong verdict, buried in its code. Unlike the dataset, this rule is chosen without justification and left unexamined, yet it sets the published number. We reproduce the official scorers of eight peer-reviewed benchmarks on five open vision-language models (VLMs) that fit a single 16 GB GPU, and introduce a blinded human-plus-LLM-judge adjudication (Cohen's kappa=0.956) that recovers what the model actually answered. The scoring rule alone moves accuracy by up to 22 points on identical outputs, yet exactly 0 wherever a model emits clean option letters, so it hides on strong-model leaderboards. It is the fallback and not the rambling that does the damage: the benchmark with the highest non-compliance we measure has an artifact of exactly zero, because its scorer abstains instead of guessing; a reasoning model with non-compliance 0.000 still swings 9.5 points with which regex match of its trace the parser keeps. No standard rule is reliable: snapping a non-answer to its closest option credits answers never given yet buries correct ones, abstention discards answers stated in words, and likelihood scoring follows answer-token priors, so a single grade conflates capability with luck rather than measuring either. We release all code, labels, and the protocol, and argue benchmarks should report a non-compliance rate and at least two rules, not one unexamined grade.

AI.brief_summary: 论文复现八个多模态 LLM 多选题基准的官方评分器，在五个开放 VLM 上用盲化人工与 LLM 评审判定模型实际答案，量化不同评分规则造成的准确率差异并审计兜底解析策略。

title: Reviso: Not All Visual Evidence Deserves Equal Attention in Video Captioning
summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can generate detailed video captions, yet they may overemphasize minor details while overlooking essential context and key events. We argue that not all visual evidence deserves equal attention, as the importance of visual information depends on the content of each video. Motivated by this observation, we propose Reviso, an agentic video captioning framework that learns what to observe and how to gather relevant visual evidence. From a low-frame-rate global preview, Reviso constructs a hierarchical Context--Focus--Points (CFP) observation plan that identifies the video context, prioritizes key aspects, and defines concrete observation targets and corresponding tools. Guided by this plan, Reviso performs goal-directed active perception by selectively revisiting temporal segments and combining tools for fine-grained inspection. It interprets the acquired evidence, updates its plan as needed, and integrates global and local information to generate the final caption. To learn this observation strategy, we develop a verification-guided pipeline that constructs high-quality training trajectories through factual verification and teacher-guided refinement. We further train Reviso using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), incorporating a key-fact reward for caption quality, a Plan Alignment Reward (PAR) for identifying important observation targets, and an Unproductive Tool-Call Penalty (UTCP) that adjusts observation-cost penalties based on caption quality. Experiments across four video captioning benchmarks show that Reviso outperforms the evaluated open-source baselines, while its generated captions better support downstream video question answering. These findings highlight the effectiveness and potential of priority-guided active observation for video captioning.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Reviso 智能体式视频描述框架：从低帧率全局预览构建分层「上下文—焦点—要点」观察计划，据此选择性回看时间片段并组合工具细查，配合可验证轨迹构建与 GRPO（含计划对齐奖励、无效工具调用惩罚）训练观察策略。
AI.relevance_reason: 与 LVR 关注的「视觉证据筛选、LOOK 与 STOP 的收益成本平衡」直接相关，其计划对齐奖励和成本惩罚可供核查如何抑制无效视觉获取、支持按需重看与停止决策。

title: SparseWAM: Driving World-Action Models are Worth 16 Register Tokens
summary: World Action Models (WAMs) transfer scene-dynamics priors to planning by jointly forecasting future scenes and ego trajectories. However, WAMs built on video generators must generate dense future videos at inference, incurring prohibitive latency, while efficient variants discard the world branch at deployment and thus forgo test-time imagination. Even when dense video latents are replaced with patch-level DINO or JEPA features, these representations still involve long token sequences and encode decision-irrelevant information. We therefore propose SparseWAM, which forecasts in a sparse register space of only 16 tokens per frame, compressed from frozen DINOv2 features and shaped by joint planning-and-scoring pretraining to concentrate decision-relevant information. Within this space, SparseWAM employs a modality-decoupled Mixture-of-Transformers with a causal attention mask that lets action tokens condition on imagined future registers, retaining explicit imagine-then-act reasoning at deployment. Its compactness further enables low-cost multimodal sampling. As a result, our SparseWAM achieves 92.6 PDMS on NAVSIM v1, 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2, and 39.6 on NavHard at only 164 ms latency, roughly 1/5 that of DriveVA, demonstrating the efficiency of the sparse register space. Code will be released upon acceptance.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 SparseWAM：把冻结 DINOv2 特征压缩为每帧仅 16 个 register token 的稀疏隐空间，并在该空间用解耦模态、带因果掩码的 Mixture-of-Transformers 让动作 token 条件于想象出的未来 register，从而在部署时保留「先想象后行动」的推理并大幅降低时延。
AI.relevance_reason: 其用联合规划-打分的预训练把决策相关信息集中到极短隐状态、并在该状态上做测试时想象的做法，可能为 LVR 的视觉信息保留、隐状态压缩与动作条件推理提供可核查的训练目标与注意力结构线索。

title: CausalPrune: Counterfactual Causal Token Pruning for Efficient Large Vision-Language Models
summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in multimodal understanding, but their practical deployment is still limited by the substantial computation introduced by excessive visual tokens. Visual token pruning offers an effective solution by removing redundant visual tokens during inference. However, existing methods typically estimate token importance from correlational statistics, which cannot distinguish tokens that causally determine the model output from those spuriously associated with it. To address this issue, we propose \textbf{CausalPrune}, a counterfactual causal token pruning framework for efficient LVLMs. We formulate LVLM inference as a Structural Causal Model and introduce the Causal Token Importance Score (CTIS), which estimates the Average Treatment Effect of intervening on each visual token. To make causal estimation practical, we derive an efficient first-order approximation of CTIS and incorporate backdoor adjustment to mitigate latent cross-modal confounding. Within this causal formulation, layer-wise causal mediation decomposes token importance into direct and indirect effects through intermediate hidden states, enabling progressive pruning across transformer layers in a principled manner. Extensive experiments on various LVLM architectures, such as LLaVA-1.5 and Qwen2.5-VL, demonstrate that CausalPrune maintains comparable or even superior multimodal performance while achieving substantial reductions in FLOPs and prefill latency, consistently outperforming existing pruning methods.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 CausalPrune，把 LVLM 推理写成结构因果模型，用反事实干预的平均处理效应估计视觉 token 的重要性，并借助一阶近似、后门调整和逐层因果中介分解实现渐进式 token 剪枝，以减少计算量。

title: Early Stopping in Large Reasoning Models: A Survey and Empirical Audit of Efficiency and Reliability
summary: Large reasoning models can improve accuracy by generating longer reasoning traces, but some of this computation may be unnecessary. Early-stopping methods aim to stop once enough reasoning is available to answer. Evaluating these methods requires accounting for the cost of deciding when to stop and the reliability of the resulting answer. We evaluate different methods across five reasoning models on mathematical and scientific reasoning, code generation, and factuality tasks by using a shared rollout replay protocol. We introduce Target-Integrated Token Efficiency (TITE) to measure efficiency relative to the oracle across accuracy targets. We also examine correctness at later exit positions, transfer across models and tasks, post-stop reasoning continuation, and retained justification quality. In our experiments, correctness can decrease at later positions beyond what the fitted decoding-noise model predicts. Reliability checks also reveal continued reasoning after forced termination and weaker supporting reasoning in some correct early-stopping outputs. The implementation can be found in https://github.com/hung20gg/audit-early-stopping.

AI.brief_summary: 该文综述并实证审计大推理模型的早停方法，在五个推理模型、数学与科学推理、代码生成和事实性任务上采用共享 rollout 重放协议进行比较，提出 TITE 指标以衡量相对 oracle 的 token 效率，并额外考察较晚退出位置的正确性、跨模型与跨任务迁移、强制停止后的继续推理以及理由质量保留。

title: On the Limits of Test-Time Compute for Self-Evaluation
summary: Self-verification and aggregation have emerged as popular approaches for bridging the gap between pass@1 and pass@N. However, increasing the number of candidates does not consistently narrow the gap between final-answer accuracy and pass@N. To understand this limitation, we use ranking error to measure how reliably models distinguish their correct generations from incorrect ones. We show that ranking error admits a bias-variance decomposition, with both components shaped by algorithmic design choices and inference compute. Across our experiments, additional compute reduces variance, while bias initially decreases before approaching a plateau. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Scorpio, a simple and general method that jointly scores randomly grouped candidates. Across math, code, and puzzle benchmarks, Scorpio improves verification, tree search, and aggregation. For verification, Scorpio improves accuracy over the strongest baseline by up to 7 percentage points while matching or exceeding that baseline's peak accuracy with 17-42% lower inference cost. For tree search, using Scorpio to score partial solutions and select the final answer improves accuracy by up to 10 percentage points over prior methods. Finally, Scorpio improves the scaling of aggregation-based methods by 11 percentage points on coding tasks.

AI.brief_summary: 论文分析自评估中测试时计算增益受限的原因，将候选排序误差分解为偏差与方差，并提出联合评分随机分组候选的 Scorpio，用于验证、树搜索与答案聚合。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及视觉或 latent 状态，但其排序误差分解和验证/聚合方法可供核查 LVR 中候选筛选、计算分配与停止决策的收益边界，尤其可能解释增加 latent 候选或算力为何主要降方差。

title: Agentic Context Management for Multi-Turn Human-AI Conversations
summary: LLMs degrade in multi-turn conversation partly because of context pollution: the model's own earlier outputs stay in context and anchor later turns, so an early misreading of the user's intent can persist after the user corrects it. Assistant omission (AO), dropping every assistant message, removes this pollution but fails when interaction is referential: later turns refer back to drafts, decisions, and tool-call results that exist only in assistant turns. We propose Agentic Conversation Context Curation (AC3), a training-free method in which a separate analyzer (1) consolidates the task specification from the user's messages alone, (2) audits the assistant's prior outputs against it, and (3) edits the context, either appending the analysis or discarding the assistant side and rebuilding the context from the specification. A second finding: pollution is contagious. An analyzer that sees the assistant's reasoning while extracting the specification can do worse than no intervention, and instructing it to ignore them did not close the gap, so we exclude assistant turns structurally. On Lost in Conversation (replaying difficulty-selected instances), where AO is an oracle by construction, AC3 closes 55-84% of the gap between full context and AO on three of four tasks and exceeds AO on the fourth, and an LLM that faithfully summarizes the history does not reproduce the gain even with more compute. On real WildChat conversations, a GPT-5-mini judge prefers AC3's next turn over both full context and AO in every configuration of our main table, though this preference depends on the judge; on CollabLLM results are mixed. In stateful tool use (tau2-bench), AO collapses to 0% on every model; AC3 does not collapse, though it falls slightly behind full context. Detector studies show that Reset removes injected pollution but is not span-selective: the gain comes from rebuilding the specification.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对多轮对话中的上下文污染问题，提出免训练的 AC3：由独立分析器仅从用户消息重建任务规范，审计助手先前输出，并据此追加分析或丢弃助手侧、按规范重建上下文。

title: A Tool in the Forward Pass: Frozen Tape Modules as Layers of a Small Language Model
comment: 12 pages, 1 figure, 9 tables. Code, configurations, results and frozen modules: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23831494
summary: Calling a tool through generated text adds decoding steps, even when the computation itself is short. We study an alternative: a small neural module that runs inside a language model's forward pass. A learned writer turns hidden states into a symbolic tape, a short sequence of discrete symbols that encodes the computation. The module, trained separately and then frozen, reduces the tape to a result, and a learned reader returns that result to the model. We evaluate arithmetic and object tracking in gemma-3-1b-it. With a writer trained on labelled tapes, the layer answers all 750 items of BIG-Bench Hard's tracking shuffled objects correctly. At seven people it needs about 1/10 of the GPU kernel time of a text-tool baseline that uses the same host model and exact code, with accuracy 1.00 against 0.99. The writer can also be learned from answers alone, guided by a hand-written copying prior, but less reliably: 5 of 6 runs succeed in the 1B host and 2 of 4 in the 4B host. Two independently trained layers keep their task accuracy when attached to one model, and a learned gate keeps them silent on the tested general-text and look-alike prompts. The results support a narrow use case: a bounded computation that returns one symbol can avoid the decoding cost of a textual tool call. Extracting the right input reliably, and deciding when to act, remain the main open problems.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在小语言模型前向过程中嵌入独立训练后冻结的「磁带」模块：由 writer 将隐藏状态写成离散符号序列，模块计算后经 reader 把结果送回模型，并在算术和物体追踪任务上评估准确率、计算成本、多模块组合与门控行为。

title: TRIAGE: Reliability- and Load-Conditioned Escalation for Two-Tier LLM Serving with a Semantic Evidence Judge
summary: Two-tier LLM serving escalates selected requests from a small model to a large one, but prompt-based routers cannot see whether retrieved evidence supports an answer, and they treat the GPU cost of an escalation as constant. We study TRIAGE, which conditions escalation on a post-generation reliability state and on a load-dependent GPU price, and we report both what held and what did not on one A40 serving Qwen2.5-7B and 32B (AWQ) under VLLM. Escalation cost rose 21.9x from 1 to 10 requests/s but showed no monotone dependence on KV-cache headroom, and a pre-registered claim that the reliability state detects corrupted evidence (AUROC>=0.70) was falsified at 0.571, although any prompt-only router scores exactly 0.500 by construction. Post hoc, a semantic evidence judge raised detection to 0.846 (0.926 on never-served items) and predicted wrong small-model answers at AUROC 0.90-0.96 on RGB and three RouterBench model pairs; the resulting cascade stayed within about 3 pp of GPT-4 at 79.5% lower API cost for GPT-3.5->GPT-4, yet fell below random routing for open-model pairs with 2-3x price ratios. End to end, the 7B->32B pair showed only a +2.88 pp held-out gap, so the allocator rightly declined to escalate and the headline is a null that a small pre-launch gate failed to expose.

title: Learning What to Ask and What to Believe: Distilling a Variational Bayesian Agent into Language Models
summary: Interactive tasks such as eliciting a user's preferences or diagnosing a hidden mechanism require an agent to track its uncertainty over a latent state, ask informative questions and act on the answers. Language models have no explicit mechanism for this, whereas Bayesian information seeking provides one through posterior inference and expected information gain (EIG), and we ask whether it can be distilled into an 8B language model. Our teacher, a lightweight Bayesian agent with a sequential variational belief and EIG query selection, matches or approaches exact and particle references on three task families. We generate synthetic interactions with the teacher on episodes disjoint from the benchmark and fine-tune \Student{} to reproduce its queries and its belief state as a structured scratchpad. On three Multi-Turn Puzzles tasks the student raises Circuit Decoding from 0.00 to 0.93 success, lowers the normalized rank of the recommended film from 0.50 to 0.10 and cuts word guessing from 32 to 3.4 attempts, exceeding the strongest reported language models on the two comparable tasks. Exposing the belief state closes much of the gap where the decision is an implicit computation rather than a read-out of the interaction; in matched teacher contrasts, EIG supervision consistently outperforms random querying, whereas greater inference fidelity does not uniformly improve the distilled student; a 70B language-model teacher does not match the Bayesian teacher in downstream student performance, and the learned skill does not transfer to an unseen task family. Variational Bayesian information seeking can thus be amortized into a language model by transferring the belief state that drives its questions and decisions.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将具备序列变分信念与 EIG 查询选择的贝叶斯教师蒸馏进 8B 语言模型，让学生用结构化 scratchpad 复现其提问与信念状态，并在三个多轮谜题任务上评测效果与消融。

title: Geometry of Confabulation and Refusal in Small Language Models
comment: 35 pages, 16 figures, 19 tables. Code, data, and the ConfabQA benchmark: https://github.com/vkazei/confabqa
summary: Faced with an unanswerable question, small language models can either refuse or confabulate: confidently produce a wrong answer. Can the hidden state before the first generated token provide a clue? Can we flip confabulations into refusals? I introduce ConfabQA, a 784-item benchmark whose obscure-pre-cutoff category breaks the typical correctness/knowledge-cutoff confound and map the geometry of the hidden state with linear probes, a sparse autoencoder (SAE), and direct optimization of intervention directions. On Qwen3-1.7B and Gemma 2 2B the probe separates upcoming refusals from confabulations well beyond prompt features (+7.4/+16.3 pp); on Llama 3.2 3B the ConfabQA margin is within fold-to-fold spread, but a direct refusal probe on PopQA and TriviaQA recovers +18-25 pp. On Qwen I closely inspect three candidate directions for the refusal vector: probe-recovered, Qwen-Scope SAE feature, and directly optimized. Although the three directions are pairwise 50-81 degrees apart, a push at or below the state's own norm along any of them flips most confabulations into refusal openings dominated by the "As..." family. Forcing the opener without touching the hidden state yields the same one-in-three judged-refusal rate as any push. The opposite push collapses refusals mostly into confabulations, yet leaves originally correct answers intact, so the direction gates the opening speech act rather than the knowledge behind it. Confabulations do not resolve into a concentrated feature in a dictionary or a token signature on Qwen3-1.7B. Scoring every probe on the margin over the strongest of four prompt-feature baselines extracts the hidden state's own contribution. Correctness signal is model-dependent and portable only for Llama 3.2 3B: 81% of the probe's margin over test majority survives transfer between ConfabQA, PopQA, and TriviaQA. Benchmark, judge, and code are released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文构建 ConfabQA 基准，用线性探针、SAE 和定向优化比较小型语言模型首 token 前隐状态中「胡编」与「拒答」的几何结构，并通过干预方向翻转输出。

title: Large language models underrepresent malice and overreport virtue
comment: 41 pages, 5 figures, 5 Extended Data figures, 2 Extended Data tables; Supplementary Information included
summary: People increasingly use large language models (LLMs) to interpret others' behaviour, often assuming that LLMs infer motives as humans do. Aligned LLMs attribute more benevolent and less malevolent motives to a whistleblower than humans do, but ratings alone cannot reveal whether these differences arise in internal representations or at report. Here we compare linear-probe readouts of LLMs' internal states with their own ratings at the same prompt position for four motives, in two preregistered studies. For the two malevolent motives, self-interest and intent to harm, internal and expressed readouts did not differ: the lower ratings reflect weaker signal along the probed directions, not suppression at output. For the two benevolent motives, duty and concern for others, expressed ratings exceeded the internal readouts, indicating amplification at report. In free text the model rarely volunteered a motive against the colleague, far less often than humans did, yet produced one readily once the scenario supplied a reason. Shifting the internal representation along a malevolent-motive direction brought both malevolent ratings to the human level, whereas the rating of duty yielded only past a threshold at which the other motives had overshot. LLMs' more charitable motive profile thus has two distinct sources: reduced malevolent signal in the probed representation and amplified benevolent attribution at report.

title: Chain-of-Thought Oversight Requires Separate Evidence for Faithfulness and Monitorability
comment: The paper is accepted by Neurips 2026 Position Track
summary: A common assumption in chain-of-thought (CoT) oversight is that a visible reasoning trace makes model behavior easier to monitor. We argue that this assumption can conflate distinct properties along a chain linking a model's internal computation, reasoning artifacts, outputs, and monitor judgments. We identify four properties along this chain: reasoning visibility (whether a trace is accessible), mechanistic faithfulness (whether a trace reflects internal computation), mechanistic localizability (whether a compact causal mechanism can be isolated), and behavioral monitorability (whether a monitor can detect the target behavior). Two complementary case studies across three open-weight reasoning models show why these distinctions matter. In the security vulnerability reasoning study, probes and activation ablations provide evidence of internal representation and causal influence, but a monitor with access to the reference answer does not outperform the majority-class baseline in a held-out test. In authority-hint factual reasoning study, a monitor correctly distinguishes changed from unchanged answers, but seven mechanistic analyses do not isolate a compact causal mechanism. These results show that evidence for one claim does not establish the others. We therefore propose an evidential-chain reporting standard. Each claim carries a licensing statement that specifies its target property, access tier, and artifact, and labels each required link as supported, unsupported, or assumed. These assessments determine whether the conclusion is licensed, conditionally licensed, or not licensed.

title: Stand-In Effects and Pooling Amplification: Design-Based Tests of Whether Biological World Models Use Actions
comment: 54 pages, 6 figures, 24 tables. Preregistrations: https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/ZXAR3 (M4) and https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/QEZBX (M5). Primary category cs.LG: a test for learned action-conditioned models; cross-listed for the statistical method (stat.ME) and the biological application (q-bio.QM)
summary: Action-conditioned world models are increasingly trained on data from randomized experiments, and whether their predictions respond to actions is usually checked by replacing or removing the actions and measuring the loss in accuracy. We show that such diagnostics report action effects where there are none: under autocorrelated designs, future actions stand in for history the model does not see, and a better model learns the stand-in better. When the design law is known, a conditional randomization test written as an e-value is valid in finite samples whatever the model, provided the resampler conditions on the full state the design used; resampling from a simpler law reproduces the false effect. We identify a second failure, specific to world models: when many sites share one action sequence (cells in a microscope field, pixels in a frame), the natural pooled score turns small model errors along the action contrast into overwhelming evidence against a true effect. In a pixel world, its median log e-value fell from $-17.3$ to $-6832$ as frames grew from 64 to 4096 pixels, while the oracle's rose. Tempering the score by a design effect estimated on training data changes the bet, not the validity. Our own preregistered analysis of optogenetic ERK experiments failed in exactly this way; a tempered statistic, selected on synthetic data and registered before the data were obtained, then rejected the null on a never-opened field ($E\approx 1.1\times10^{10}$). Every analysis is preregistered, fixed in a dated protocol before it was run, or labelled exploratory, and every reported result is generated from hashed result files.

title: Delivered, Not Used: Evaluating Agent Memory at Its Point of Use
summary: Task success, retrieval quality, and cost do not show whether an LLM agent used a delivered memory or what followed from that use. We introduce MemUse, which evaluates memory at its point of use in recorded trajectories: each memory delivery is compared with what the agent could already see and followed through the agent's later actions and their consequences. An agentic judge rates each delivered entry's relevance, accuracy, novelty, influence, and observed effect; programmatic checks enforce complete reading of cited evidence, and fixed rules aggregate the ratings into verdicts linked to memory histories and delivery cost. On 8,000 SWE-bench Verified episodes from three memory systems, resolve rates stay within 0.4 percentage points of a no-memory baseline, yet MemUse shows that most delivered entries were irrelevant, most relevant entries went unused, and in two systems most deliveries restated content the agent could still see. It also surfaces effects that outcomes hide: 23.2\% of episodes with beneficial memory use still failed, and 5 of 16 with harmful use still succeeded.
