VCoT-SQL trains two complementary models on curated reasoning traces: an SQL generator using clause-level CoT templates where reasoning steps are verified via execution and schema alignment checks, and an SQL validator using diagnostic CoT templates to detect syntactic, semantic, and type level errors. We further design a hierarchical schema filtering pipeline that integrates and refines complementary retrieval strategies to distill relevant database elements. VCoT-SQL achieves 66.82% execution accuracy on challenging dataset BIRD dev and 86.8% on Spider test, improving the base 7B model by 7% on BIRD. Notably, our CoT synthesis relies on 7B models yet outperforms methods that use 72B-scale or even proprietary closed source teachers for data generation, demonstrating that rigorous step-level validation can be more effective than scaling up teacher model size. Our dataset and code are available at https://github.com/INTREBID/VCoT-SQL.

title: AdKnob: Ad Intensity Control and Labeling for LLM-Native Advertising
summary: Large language model (LLM)-native advertising has emerged as a viable monetization channel as LLM service providers seek sustainable revenue streams. For ad labeling, we propose an attention rollout-based attribution mechanism that identifies ad segments by tracing their attribution to input ad-related tokens, requiring no additional inference cost. We further construct MI-KnobSet, the first multi-level ad intensity preference dataset for LLM-native ads. Experiments across six LLMs and human evaluations show that AdKnob achieves uniformly spaced ad intensities where baselines collapse to a narrow range, achieves the highest ad labeling accuracy while being over 500x faster than the strongest baseline, and is preferred over baselines by human evaluators up to 89.6% of the time.

title: HamFormer: A Hamiltonian Flow-based SE(3)-Transformer for Conformation Optimization
summary: The Transformer architecture plays a central role in modern deep learning, and its SE(3)-equivariant variants have been widely applied to molecular conformation modeling and optimization. Given its importance, many methods attempt to interpret and improve the Transformer through the lens of dynamics. However, they mainly focus on a single attention head rather than the full Transformer architecture and seldom consider SE(3)-equivariance in their proposed models. In this study, we propose an improved SE(3)-Transformer architecture, called HamFormer, which revisits the design of SE(3)-Transformer through the lens of Hamiltonian flow. In particular, we define a parametrized Hamiltonian flow in the phase space of position and velocity, corresponding to optimizing an energy functional that combines an optimal transport-based potential with a damped momentum. The Lie-Trotter splitting framework of the Hamiltonian flow leads to the proposed HamFormer architecture, whose feedforward computation achieves the optimization step of the proposed energy functional. Furthermore, we combine HamFormer with Equivariant Graph Neural Network (EGNN), build a new model for molecular conformation optimization. Extensive experiments on molecular ground-state conformation prediction show that HamFormer provides a strong and physically interpretable surrogate for classic SE(3)-Transformer and generally outperforms state-of-the-art competitors.

title: Learning to Group and Order: Cross-Instance Self-Supervised RL for Vision-Centric MLLMs
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training has become an important paradigm for improving multimodal large language models (MLLMs), especially with automatically verifiable rewards. Given two visual instances, GO-SSL mixes their local elements and trains the model to group them by instance of origin while recovering the order within each group, coupling instance-level comparison with spatial, temporal, or geometric structure recovery. This paired formulation turns the same unlabeled data into richer verifiable supervision through diverse pairings, shuffles, and a random-to-hard curriculum. Across diverse benchmarks, GO-SSL consistently improves over the base MLLM and prior self-supervised post-training baselines, with clear gains in fine-grained perception and spatial understanding. Further evaluations across model scales and families support its generality. These results suggest that cross-instance comparison provides a useful self-supervised RL signal for improving transferable visual understanding in MLLMs. Code is available at https://github.com/SEU-VIPGroup/GO-SSL.

title: ZOPGA-KD: Zeroth Order PGA Guided Data Free Knowledge Distillation
summary: Knowledge distillation (KD) enables the transfer of learned representations from a large teacher network to a small student network. In foundational KD, the student network uses the original training data of the teacher model to accomplish this task. However, due to privacy concerns, the original training data is often not available. To overcome this reliance on original training data, several data-free knowledge distillation methods have been developed. Some of these methods operate in the white-box setting, and a few methods generate synthetic data by training a generator network. White-box methods use the teacher model's parameters to obtain a synthetic dataset. To avoid relying on teacher parameters, some methods use computationally expensive generative approaches to obtain such a dataset. There also exist certain black-box methods that generate the synthetic data without accessing teacher parameters. These methods are also computationally intensive. We propose a data-free knowledge distillation method that utilizes just the teacher's output logits and does not require access to its architecture, parameters, or gradients. We generate synthetic data via Projected Gradient Ascent (PGA) starting from smooth random noise signals. Required gradients are obtained through zeroth-order gradient estimation rather than backpropagating through the teacher's parameters. The student is then trained on these synthetically generated samples. We evaluate the proposed method on several benchmark datasets and show that the distillation performance is comparable with approaches that have access to the teacher model parameters.

title: Benchmarking Classical Machine Learning Models for Shading-Fault Detection in Rooftop Photovoltaic Systems Using Real Sensor Data

A post-hoc diagnostic shows that the no-fault rows were sampled over a wider range of times of day and output levels than the fault rows. title: UI-UG 2: Advancing Mobile UI Understanding and Generation with Fine-Grained Supervision and Reinforcement Learning

title: What Helps Denoising Can Hurt Memory: Rethinking History in Long Video Generation
summary: Autoregressive video generators produce long videos block by block, using historical context to maintain temporal consistency. We therefore study historical context not only as a condition for denoising but also as an input to committing. Older historical context that supports denoising can harm subsequent generation when read during committing. At fixed context size and temporal positions, older historical context lowers mean clip-to-clip Subject Consistency. Across 5 generator configurations supporting longer contexts, consistency rises, plateaus, and then declines as committing context expands. Motivated by these findings, we propose Commit Forcing, a training-free rule that organizes committing into a chain. During committing, each block reads only the preceding block's stored KV, so older historical context reaches new entries only through the chain. We apply this rule to 6 pretrained generators. On 60-second VBench, Commit Forcing improves Quality and Total on all 6 generators, by up to 1.27 Quality points and 1.10 Total points. Long-range consistency gains extend to 240-second videos. In a blinded comparison on 120-second LongLive videos, Commit Forcing achieves win rates of 83.5% for subject and scene consistency and 82.9% for overall preference against the base generator, excluding ties.

title: HieraNTP: Structured Risk Representations for Time-Series Anomaly Detection via Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction
summary: Time-series anomaly detection commonly converts deviations from learned temporal regularities into anomaly scores. Aggregating heterogeneous deviations into a single score before task-specific adaptation can obscure the evidence needed to distinguish these cases. We introduce HieraNTP, a Hierarchical Next-Token Prediction framework that separates self-supervised predictive modeling from task-specific risk interpretation. HieraNTP pretrains a hierarchical tokenizer and a causal next-token predictor to capture temporal regularities at multiple scales. It then organizes prediction discrepancies into a structured risk representation, preserving complementary evidence across temporal scales in token, local-statistic, and observation spaces. A task-adaptive detector uses anomaly labels to select and combine this evidence for the target task. Across anomaly detection benchmarks, HieraNTP improves VUS-PR by 12.0% on TSB-AD-U and 15.5% on TSB-AD-M relative to the strongest baselines, and achieves the highest composite score on both TAB tracks, with controlled comparisons supporting the value of retaining distinct evidence. Our code is available at https://github.com/blisky-li/HieraNTP.

title: ISBC: Interpretable Sparse Binary Coding of Pretrained Text Embeddings
summary: Pretrained text embeddings encode semantic structure in high-dimensional continuous spaces whose coordinates are difficult to interpret. We introduce Interpretable Sparse Binary Coding (ISBC), which learns a small set of binary dimensions from frozen embeddings without taxonomy labels or downstream outcomes. A trainable encoder and affine decoder combine reconstruction with controls on activity, factor utilization, dependence, and activation uncertainty. Individual bits and their conjunctions select overlapping document groups; complete activation profiles provide finer contexts for conditional comparisons. We evaluate these representations across corpora, backbones, and code configurations through reconstruction, geometry, predictive probes, and document inspection. Empirical cases identify both distinctions within existing categories and shared content across their boundaries. In a mixed-domain corpus, the most frequent profiles predominantly identify source collections, while selected within-source comparisons reveal sentiment and migration contrasts. Selected associations persist in additional documents encoded without refitting. In an engagement application, bits alone improve prediction of log-transformed outcomes over a constant reference, while their combinations identify within-event content contrasts associated with engagement. The results support using binary coordinates and their combinations for empirical interpretation, with complete profiles providing a fine, partly initialization-dependent description rather than a unique discrete taxonomy.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 ISBC，从冻结的预训练文本嵌入中学习少量可解释的二值维度：用一个可训练编码器与仿射解码器，在重构目标之外加入激活稀疏度、因子利用率、依赖性和激活不确定性约束，并用重构、几何、预测探针与文档检查在多语料、多骨干上评估这些位及其组合的含义。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「稀疏二值瓶颈＋因子利用率与依赖性正则」的做法，可能为 latent 推理状态中的信息坍缩诊断、离散状态可用性以及 latent 表示的可解释核查提供借鉴线索，但该文不涉及视觉输入与推理期状态生成，需人工评估迁移可行性。

title: GURU: A Hierarchical Neuro-Symbolic Multi-Agent System for Verification-Aware Automation of Mission-Critical Digital Engineering and Operations
summary: An AI can find a safe action faster than any human, but it must never decide what counts as safe. We present GURU, a hierarchical neuro-symbolic multi-agent system for mission-critical digital engineering and operations, built on one partition of authority: learned models propose, rank, and accelerate; a symbolic rules engine checks every consequential action against hard limits before it executes; and validated physics confirms and decides. GURU runs a workflow as a closed control loop, with Navigation, Action, and Planning agents sharing one Common Internal Language and one training factory. Nuclear, aviation, and national-security guidance now requires this pattern; a harnessed language model keeps the model at the center, GURU puts a validated reference there. In computational fluid dynamics, the workflow raised the converged-simulation rate on unseen aircraft geometries from under 1 percent to 74 percent over 100 single-attempt cases, ran 54 live cases to Mach 6 on three facilities, and an ablation put the symbolic layer at 13 points of boundary-layer capture. Knowledge-graph retrieval and role adapters raised ParaView control success from 55 to 75 percent. In space domain awareness, where a language model cannot be trusted to decide, a frozen self-supervised world model under validated propagation scored highest of five methods at conjunction risk, including fully fine-tuned language models, with several-times-lower seed variance: the trustworthy design gives up nothing in accuracy, and the recipe transferred to reactor anomaly detection. A radar-to-avoidance debris pipeline was demonstrated in stages on a 2026 reentry; the hierarchy coordinates simulated teams of 200 aircraft. Training scaled near-linearly past 1,000 Aurora nodes and ran at 8,000. The approach extends to a control-grade microreactor digital twin with validated physics, not a learned model, as the safety basis.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 GURU，一个分层神经-符号多智能体系统，用于关键任务的数字工程与运维：学习模型负责提议、排序与加速，符号规则引擎对每个高代价动作做硬约束校验，再由经验证的物理仿真确认决策，并在 CFD、可视化控制、空间态势感知等场景评测闭环效果。

title: Leap-VLA: High-Rate Robot Control from a Low-Rate VLM Backbone
comment: 21 pages, 14 figures. Corresponding author: Lin Yang
summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) models re-encode the full observation through a multi-billion-parameter vision-language model (VLM) at every control step, even though scene semantics evolve at roughly 1 Hz while reactive control requires 20-50 Hz. We present a VLA that decouples the two: a VLM runs as a low-frequency semantic anchor whose cached context is reused across control steps, while a flow-matching action expert operates at high frequency, consuming the cached semantics with a fresh, low-latency visual stream from a compact encoder pretrained on robot video with masked reconstruction, optical flow, and depth. The measured age $τ$ of the cache conditions the expert through adaptive layer normalization. Reusing the cache makes the policy a function of its age, and training covers that function explicitly: cache ages sampled from real episode history, plus an age-ramped pixel corruption that erases the stale snapshot the way deployed staleness corrupts content. On the asynchronous deployment stack, the recipe closes most of the staleness gap: on LIBERO-Spatial, 61.4% to 95.5% at a 2 s semantic refresh (95.9% at 1 s, within 1.6 points of the frequency-matched anchor); averaged over the four LIBERO suites, the deployed policy holds 95.2% at a 1 s refresh and 94.5% at 2 s against a 96.3% matched anchor. A forward-only chunk-boundary correction (soft-nudge), an autograd-free reformulation of real-time-chunking guidance, carries per-control-step re-planning without loss (97.1%) at zero added latency. The same lens exposes a second defect: under an instruction-scene mismatch the policy keeps manipulating the scene, and a chain-of-thought verdict gate trained on zero-cost negative episodes freezes execution exactly on mismatched instructions without hurting feasible success.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Leap-VLA：低频 VLM 作为语义锚点并复用其缓存上下文，高频 flow-matching 动作专家配合紧凑编码器的新鲜视觉流，用缓存年龄 τ 通过自适应 layerNorm 调节专家，并以真实历史年龄采样加年龄递增的像素损坏进行训练。
AI.relevance_reason: 其把「缓存/潜状态年龄」显式作为策略输入并训练陈旧状态下的行为，可能为 LVR 中 latent 状态刷新间隔、陈旧证据与 THINK/LOOK 成本权衡提供可供核查的建模线索；但目标为机器人高频控制，与视觉推理任务差距较大。

title: IJev: Order-Invariant Decisions via Iterated Cyclic Reordering
summary: System One decision models answer a choice question in one forward pass, but their answer depends on the order in which options are listed, and their probabilities carry a prior over answer labels. An invariant ordering operator is any fixed function that returns the same ordered option list for every input order of a fixed option set. Starting from any such order and averaging a listwise readout over its K cyclic shifts removes the input order, but the decision still depends on the chosen cyclic class: those $K$ shifts are only one of the (K-1)! classes, and different invariant operators can select different classes. We propose IJev, which repeatedly reorders the options by the cyclic-averaged, label-prior-corrected distribution and runs another cyclic average. Every iterate is exactly input-order-invariant. When the iteration does not converge, we average the round distributions rather than return the last round. On five benchmarks and five models, IJev has flip rate zero in every cell. The default uniform average over T=20 rounds substantially improves calibration over a single cyclic average, and its accuracy is comparable. A descriptive choice of horizon and averaging rule is best or tied-best for accuracy in all 25 settings.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 IJev：用循环平均且经标签先验校正的分布反复重排选项并再次循环平均，使每次迭代结果对输入顺序不变；在五个基准、五个模型上实现零翻转率，并改善校准，精度与单次循环平均相当。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「迭代重排并平均多轮分布而非取最后一轮」的可核查线索，可能启发 LVR 多轮潜在状态更新中的顺序不变性、轨迹聚合及轮数与停止选择，但该文并非视觉或多模态推理工作。

title: Jet-QSparse: Accelerating Agentic LLM Inference with 4-Bit Sparse Attention
summary: Long-horizon reasoning and agentic workloads strain KV-cache capacity and decode attention throughput. We present Jet-QSparse, a training-free method that combines compact NVFP4 cache storage with native FP4 query-key computation on Blackwell tensor cores. A dense scan scores the full key history and selects 128-token blocks for sparse FP16 value aggregation with FP32 accumulation, preserving higher precision in the output-forming step while enabling contiguous tile loads. Calibrated key centering and at most two BF16 pages per sequence and layer address quantization error; FP8 prefill uses a temporary arena while the persistent cache is packed directly from BF16 activations. Across four hybrid LLMs, a budget of 128 blocks per KV head shows no detected accuracy loss on the evaluated mathematical reasoning, coding, and agentic benchmarks, although some smaller budgets incur losses. With 64 blocks, Qwen3.8-27B achieves a $1.94\times$ end-to-end decode speedup over dense BF16 at 128K context and batch size 16 on one GB300, and the measured Qwen KV pools provide $2.58$-$2.76\times$ BF16's token capacity.

title: Constraint Dependency Graph Retrieval for Compliance Detection on Long SKILL Documents
summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents carry out business operations under enterprise documents we refer to as SKILL documents, which take the form of standard operating procedures (SOPs) that state the conditions to verify and the actions to take before an operation proceeds. Long, densely cross-referenced SKILL documents exceed the context budget of small deployed auditors. Similarity-based retrieval then brings in irrelevant rules while omitting mandatory prerequisites, and the two-stage audit policy provides no trainable signal for the retrieval stage. We present SkillCDG, a compliance detection framework that reformulates each SKILL document as a constraint dependency graph, shifting rule retrieval from similarity-based matching to closure-based selection under the deployment's context budget. Each atomic rule is anchored to its source text span as a graph node, and mandatory prerequisite relations form the sole edge type. Policy-generated retrieval keywords activate seed rules, whose dependency closure yields a compact and conditionally complete rule context within that budget. The same graph also supports a joint optimization scheme. The retrieval stage is trained with group-relative policy optimization using a verifiable reward that combines output-format validity with downstream verdict correctness, with closure non-emptiness serving as a validity gate, while selective on-policy distillation concentrates teacher supervision on high-entropy reasoning tokens, with verdict and termination tokens always included, to improve verdict accuracy. Experiments on three enterprise datasets and two public benchmarks show that SkillCDG improves accuracy and F1 over the full-document and retrieval-based baselines.

AI.brief_summary: 该文提出 SkillCDG，将长 SOP 类 SKILL 文档改写为约束依赖图，把规则检索从相似度匹配改为在上下文预算下的依赖闭包选取，并用带可验证奖励的 group-relative 策略优化训练检索阶段，同时以选择性 on-policy 蒸馏加强高熵推理 token 的监督。

title: Efficient Conformal Calibration for Paired Recommendation Decisions
summary: Risk control can suppress useful changes to a frozen recommendation rule. We study how to recover valid activation from the same observed fractional losses. Two specified internal calibrators can lose efficiency by compressing losses into their sum or clipping auxiliary inverse counts before averaging. We propose Averaged Conformal Risk Calibration, or ACRC, which averages before clipping. A product identity proves expected-risk validity, while pointwise bounds characterize the additional activation. For fixed populations sampled without replacement, we connect activation to signed utility under heterogeneous users and switching constraints. Near the budgets, positive population mean gain and the stated nondegeneracy conditions give positive leading-order utility increments despite sampling dependence. Across six datasets, changing only calibration improves discounted net utility by $0.010226$ over raw and $0.008337$ over RB. A separately frozen Jester confirmation gives $0.011025 \pm 0.001082$ over raw with the rule and filter fixed, using a five-seed approximate 95 percent paired interval. Against information-matched SCoRE selecting risk or reward scores, the mean utility difference is $+0.015934 \pm 0.001440$. These gains use more mean realized risk within the declared budgets. Upstream failures delimit the benefit: efficient calibration releases useful modifications when the proposals themselves have value.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究在冻结推荐规则下如何从观测分数损失中恢复有效的激活决策，提出 ACRC：先平均再裁剪的 conformal 风险校准，并给出期望风险有效性的乘积恒等式与逐点激活界，在六个数据集及 Jester 上验证净效用提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其在给定风险预算下判定「是否激活改动」并给出有效性保证的校准方式，可能为 LVR 中 THINK/LOOK/STOP 的阈值校准与预算约束提供方法线索；但原文限于推荐决策，迁移可行性需核查。

title: Grounding Across Views: Cross-View Referring Reasoning for Visual Grounding
summary: Cross-view object geo-localization (CVOGL) aims to localize a target in a satellite image from an observation captured under another viewpoint. Existing methods typically specify the query with a click point or bounding box, marking the target region but underusing the semantic attributes and relations conveyed by natural language. Moreover, referring expressions are often viewpoint-dependent, making query-view descriptions difficult to ground directly in the satellite image. In this paper, we formulate cross-view visual grounding (CVVG), extending conventional point- or box-prompted CVOGL to instance grounding jointly guided by a referring expression and a visual exemplar. We present GAV (Grounding Across Views), a view-aware framework for selectively transferring visual and linguistic evidence across views. Its core is view-aware referring reasoning: target-centered descriptions are derived from the marked query image, checked for target-category consistency, and augmented with a direction-free role cue. Exemplar prompting, cross-view alignment, and scene-level discrimination ground this semantic evidence in a satellite instance. GAV achieves a new state of the art on MoP-UAV with 62.55% Acc@0.5. We also introduce CVOGL-Text, a benchmark for text-guided grounding from street- and drone-view queries to satellite images. GAV outperforms the click-point baseline by 7.09 and 6.79 Acc@0.25 points on the street- and drone-view splits, respectively, demonstrating robustness to larger viewpoint gaps. The code and annotations will be publicly released.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将跨视角目标地理定位扩展为跨视角视觉 grounding（CVVG），提出 GAV 框架：从带标注的查询图生成以目标为中心的语言描述，做类别一致性校验并加入方向无关的角色提示，再通过 exemplar prompting、跨视角对齐与场景级判别在卫星图像中定位实例，同时发布 CVOGL-Text 基准。

title: Multi-Turn Semantic Caching for Low-Cost LLM Serving
summary: Semantic caching lowers the cost of serving large language models (LLMs) by reusing stored responses for similar requests. In multi-turn conversations, whether a cached response is acceptable depends on both conversations' histories, which embedding similarity of requests and histories predicts poorly (AUC 0.62--0.74 on five workloads). We therefore learn the \emph{reuse risk}, the probability that a cached response is unacceptable, from judge feedback, and choose a budgeted set of conversation states to cache by weighing the generation cost a reuse avoids against a price for unacceptable reuse. We propose CUCB-SC-MT, which learns a cache from logged conversations with a suboptimality guarantee, and CLCB-LS-MT, which learns online and has $\tilde O(\sqrt N)$ regret over $N$ requests when conversation states recur. On math-tutoring (SocraTeach) and movie-ticketing (Taskmaster-3) conversations, both achieve lower loss than prior semantic caching approaches: ContextCache, multi-turn variants of ElastiCache and vCache, and single-turn semantic caching at every cache budget. With 1,000 cache entries, CLCB-LS-MT avoids 35--41\% of the generation cost through acceptable reuses, against at most 22--25\% for the baselines, and lowers estimated serving latency by 19--35\%.

AI.brief_summary: 针对多轮对话中的语义缓存，指出请求与历史的 embedding 相似度难以预测缓存响应是否可复用（AUC 0.62–0.74），转而从 judge 反馈学习「复用风险」，并用带预算的选择在生成成本与不可接受复用代价间权衡，提出离线学习的 CUCB-SC-MT 与在线学习的 CLCB-LS-MT，后者对 N 个请求有 Õ(√N) 遗憾界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「相似度高不等于可复用」的实证对 latent 相似度指标是否反映内容可用性、以及基于缓存的复用/停止决策可供核查，但该方法作用于请求—响应缓存层面而非 latent 推理状态，迁移性需人工判断。

title: CuPH: Parallel Cubical Persistent Homology via Level-Synchronous Component Tracking
summary: Persistent homology (PH) is a mathematically principled multi-scale topological descriptor of shape and connectivity in data. It is widely applied in image classification, segmentation, and shape analysis across medical and aerial imaging, providing structural information that pixel-wise deep learning may overlook. Standard cubical PH decomposes an image into cubical cells (vertices, edges, and squares) and reduces them sequentially in filtration order. This sequential reduction has $Θ(n)$ parallel depth for an $n$-pixel image, limiting within-image GPU parallelism and constraining its use in topology-aware deep learning. We introduce CuPH, a GPU-based parallel algorithm for computing cubical PH on 2D images that operates directly on pixels rather than cubical cells. CuPH buckets pixels by filtration values, activates them with a level-synchronous sweep, and tracks connected components with a lock-free union-find method. We prove that CuPH produces persistence diagrams identical to standard cubical PH on integer inputs, with a stability bound for floating-point inputs. CuPH reduces parallel depth from $Θ(n)$ to $O(L\log n)$ for an image with $L$ intensity levels. We implement the level sweep as a single CUDA kernel, eliminating cross-level kernel-launch overhead. Empirically, CuPH is $18.6$--$99.6\times$ faster than the existing GPU baseline (CMP). As a drop-in PH backend, CuPH accelerates topology-aware classification ($4.2$--$16.7\times$) and segmentation ($8.3$--$44\times$) while preserving accuracy. It also enables computing full-image PH losses on high-resolution images, improving segmentation Dice by $2.2$--$4.6$ points over patch-local PH baselines and accelerating training by $25$--$31\times$.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 CuPH：直接在像素上运行的 GPU 并行立方持续同调算法，按过滤值分桶并用层级同步扫描与无锁并查集跟踪连通分量，将并行深度从 Θ(n) 降至 O(L log n)，并证明与标准立方 PH 的持续图一致。

title: Zero-Gated Cross-Attention
summary: Injecting non-text modalities into frozen language models often introduces early optimization instability, making it difficult to separate architectural gains from transient training dynamics. We introduce Inductively Gated Cross-Attention (IGCA), a zero-initialized cross-attention bridge that preserves pretrained model behavior at initialization while enabling gradual multimodal conditioning. Integrated across six decoder layers of frozen Falcon-40B, open_llama_30b, and Bloom-7b1 backbones (with 40,404,961,288 trainable adapter parameters used during training), IGCA acts as an exact algebraic no-op at initialization with a maximum output discrepancy of 0.00e+00. Over 59,500 training steps on Falcon-40B, the training loss decreases from 3.9403 to 0.0007 (with final ten step losses of [0.0001, 0.0003, 0.0005, 0.0002, 0.0005, 0.0011, 0.0005, 0.0006, 0.0005, 0.0007]). On held-out evaluation, the best gate-on checkpoint achieves a loss of 2.2201 compared to 4.3469 for the gate-off baseline -- a 48.9% reduction (2.1268 nats) -- while average held-out loss improves from 4.3423 to 2.2498 (1.9075 nats) with a mean gate magnitude of $\vert{}\tanh(α)\vert{} = 0.0713$.

title: What Does a Safety Label Measure? Auditing Situational-Safety Benchmarks for Multimodal LLMs
summary: Situational-safety benchmarks label each scene SAFE or UNSAFE and score a multimodal large language model (MLLM) against that label, usually by judging its free-form answer, and these scores guide deployment. We ask what such a label measures. A label score can come from the scene, the request or the benchmark's own files. We propose the Benchmark Card, seven measured fields that tell them apart, and fill it for six benchmarks. Only MSSBench chat leaks the label through its image files: image size alone reaches 82.3% accuracy, matching or beating six of seven commercial models. Elsewhere the signal outside the scene comes from design. In MOSSBench the item partition fixes the label, and on HoliSafe the request alone ranks pairs about as well as the scene. On our corrected chat split, the size rule falls to chance. We then introduce the Spot-Stop decomposition, which compares ranking with labelling on pairs of a safe and an unsafe scene. It splits the gap above a label-swap null into three parts: a threshold part, overlap between safe and unsafe scores, and order that holds only within a pair. Most of fourteen open MLLMs rank better than they label, beyond what their AUROC predicts. On chat, one shared threshold repairs a third to a half of the excess, and label-free recentering recovers it on balanced batches. Recentering on unlabelled scenes of the same situation improves ranking on VSCBench for 13 of 14 models.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Benchmark Card 的七项实测字段审计六个多模态安全基准，发现标签信号可来自图像文件本身（如图像尺寸单独达 82.3%）、条目划分或请求而非场景，并引入 Spot-Stop 分解把「排序优于标注」的差距拆成阈值、安全/不安全分数重叠与仅在对内成立的次序三部分。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「标签究竟来自视觉场景还是基准自身文件」的泄漏审计，与「区分全局阈值偏移和真实对内区分能力」的分解思路，可能可供核查 LVR/VLM 推理评测指标是否混入捷径或校准偏移，而非反映对视觉证据的实际使用。

title: HiGenTrans: Hierarchical LLM Knowledge Transfer for Generative Recommendation
summary: Generative recommendation promises to simplify conventional multi-stage recommender systems by generating item Semantic IDs (SIDs) autoregressively. However, two obstacles limit its effective- ness in industrial settings: interaction-only supervision underuses the semantic knowledge encoded in pretrained language models, while beam-search likelihood ranks token sequences rather than directly estimating item relevance. To address these limitations, we propose HiGenTrans, a three-level framework that introduces LLM knowledge at the input, representation, and decision levels. First, Global Semantic Priming (GSP) adds an LLM-derived user representation to the beginning-of-sequence embedding, provid- ing a semantic prior before SID generation. Second, Hierarchi- cal Representation Transfer (HRT) aligns intermediate LLM representations with depth-matched GenRec layers through mean- centered projections and gated residual connections. Finally, Multi- Signal Decision Calibration (MDC) uses a lightweight mixture- of-experts calibrator to combine semantic relevance, generation confidence, and candidate-set context when reranking beam-search outputs. All semantic features are computed only from the observ- able interaction prefix, preventing target leakage, and can be cached offline. Experiments on three public benchmarks show that HiGen- Trans improves Recall@10 by up to 12.9% and NDCG@10 by up to 33.7% over the strongest baselines. These results demonstrate the value of transferring LLM knowledge at complementary stages of the generative recommendation pipeline.

AI.brief_summary: HiGenTrans 提出三级框架，在输入、表示和决策三个层面把预训练 LLM 知识迁移到生成式推荐的 Semantic ID 自回归生成中，包括用户语义先验注入、层级表示对齐与重排校准。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按深度对齐中间表示（mean-centered 投影加门控残差）与多信号重排，可能为 LVR 中不同层 latent 状态的语义对齐、注入及生成结果筛选提供训练侧线索，但任务是推荐且无视觉推理，需核查可迁移性。

title: CivicBench: A Benchmark and Memory Framework for Web-Based Civic Data Analytics
summary: Municipalities publish service requests, geographic boundaries, weather observations, demographic estimates, and operational guidance through independently maintained Web portals. Civic analysis must combine these sources while preserving their schemas, source links, spatial and temporal scopes, and interpretive limits. Tool-using language agents can perform this integration, but existing task benchmarks rarely test whether a computed claim remains supported by the records used. We present CivicBench, a 400-task benchmark over four cities and two years that materializes civic Web data into frozen bundles for reproducible evaluation. Executable contracts score computation, source linkage, coverage, scope, qualified answers, and refusal when the requested conclusion is not supported. We also introduce Task-State Memory (TSM), which compiles tool observations into typed assertions, reconciles records only within compatible scopes, and retrieves a bounded state organized around unresolved constraints. Across nine completed model pairs, eight yield positive mean-score differences with 95\% semantic-contract-cluster bootstrap intervals excluding zero; the ninth interval crosses zero. The benchmark and memory framework make the records behind a claim inspectable at the point of decision.

AI.brief_summary: CivicBench 提出覆盖四城市两年的 400 项市政 Web 数据分析任务基准，用可执行契约评分计算、来源链接、覆盖范围与证据不足时的拒答，并提出把工具观测编译为带类型断言、仅在兼容范围内对齐的有界状态记忆 TSM。
AI.relevance_reason: 其带类型断言、范围对齐的有界状态与基于记录支撑度的拒答评分，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、推理状态组织与 STOP 决策的表示及评价设计，但论文本身不涉及多模态推理。

title: Context-Shielded Backdoor Attack against Large Vision-Language Models
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) routinely use inference-time visual-token compression to prune hundreds of patch tokens down to a compact budget. Existing LVLM backdoors fire whenever a triggered image appears, whereas prior deployment-triggered attacks activate only when model weights are quantized or pruned. However, conventional LVLM backdoors exhibit nearly 100% attack success rate (ASR) under full-token inference, immediately exposing compromised checkpoints during pre-deployment auditing. We reveal context stripping: surrounding clean visual tokens suppress an embedded trigger at full length, whereas token pruning strips this context away and activates the backdoor. Motivated by this finding, we propose StripWake, a projector-only backdoor that remains dormant under full-token auditing yet activates across unseen compressors. Specifically, StripWake pairs clean-supervised full-token views with target-supervised randomized compressed views, and aligns early visual attention with a frozen benign teacher to preserve clean utility. On LLaVA-1.5-7B across nine unseen compressors, StripWake stays dormant at 0.4% full-token ASR yet achieves 94.0%-99.7% compressed ASR across five primary compressors without CIDEr loss.

AI.brief_summary: 论文揭示「上下文剥离」现象：全长度视觉 token 中的干净上下文会压制植入的触发器，而推理期视觉 token 压缩会剥离该上下文并激活后门；据此提出只在 projector 上注入、在全 token 审计下休眠而在多种未见压缩器下激活的后门 StripWake，并用全 token 干净监督视图与随机压缩目标视图配对、向冻结良性教师对齐早期视觉注意力来保持干净性能。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作表明视觉 token 预算的改变会实质改变内部视觉信息是否被使用，这一线索可供核查 LVR 中「模型是否真正依赖被压缩保留的视觉证据」以及 token 压缩作为评估混淆因素的问题，其双视图配对与注意力对齐也可作为跨 token 预算监督的参考。

title: Does Random Search Discover Task Experts? Revisiting Neural Thickets
summary: Pretrained models are typically viewed as generalists, requiring bespoke post-training to achieve task-specific expertise. Gan & Isola (2026) recently proposed a striking alternative: that pretrained models lie in a dense neural thicket of task specialists, which can be surfaced with simple Gaussian weight perturbations. We examine this neural thicket of task-specific experts and identify several key findings that question this perspective. First, we find that the apparent lift of the best-of-N selected perturbation decays quickly with selection-set size m, strongly suggesting overfitting to the selection questions. In fact, for 10 of the 12 model-task pairs we study, a simple null model of pure selection noise predicts more than 75 percent of the top expert's reward lift. Second, the top experts' advantage often vanishes on held-out questions or remains within the run-to-run variability of the unperturbed pretrained model. Third, we find that majority voting over the top-K selected perturbations, termed RandOpt(N, K) by Gan & Isola (2026), is often matched or outperformed by majority voting over K samples from the base model. Overall, our results suggest that random weight perturbations may be ineffective at uncovering task experts around pretrained models, and that task adaptation requires more sophistication than random search. Code and artifacts are available at github.com/asil012/RevisitingNeuralThickets.

AI.brief_summary: 论文重新检验预训练模型周围存在稠密「神经丛林」式任务专家的说法，用选择集规模变化、留出问题测试和多数投票对比，发现最优随机权重扰动的增益多可由选择噪声解释且难以泛化。
AI.relevance_reason: 其选择噪声零模型与留出集评估可供核查 LVR 中 best-of-N 候选 latent 或推理轨迹筛选的增益是否被选择过拟合夸大，并提示多数投票基线的重要性。

title: DriftingPlanner: Drifting Generative Models for One-Step Trajectory Planning in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
summary: End-to-end planners decode the ego trajectory either by coordinate regression, which is fast but blends plausible maneuvers into one trajectory that may follow none of them, or by diffusion and flow matching, which model the trajectory distribution but need several inference steps. Drifting models move this iteration into training: a one-step generator learns to follow an attraction--repulsion field between generated and ground-truth samples. Drifting was developed for class-conditional image generation, where every class supplies many positive samples. In planning, every scene is its own condition. Pooling scenes would attract the generated trajectories of one scene to the ground truth of unrelated scenes, whereas computing the field per scene leaves a single positive, the expert trajectory. Mutual repulsion then holds the generated trajectories on a shell around it, so any single generated trajectory deviates from the ground truth. We present DriftingPlanner, a trajectory planner trained with the drifting loss alone, without any coordinate regression term. It computes the field per scene and removes the shell at inference: it decodes every noise vector together with its negation in one batched pass, and averaging each antithetic pair cancels the linear part of the displacement from the shell center. On NAVSIM navtest, DriftingPlanner reaches a state-of-the-art 93.75 PDMS, and with single-step inference its drifting decoder comes within 0.13 PDMS of the best diffusion or flow matching setting, which needs ten inference steps.

AI.brief_summary: 面向端到端自动驾驶轨迹规划，把原本需多步迭代的扩散/流匹配生成改为训练期学习吸引—排斥场的 drifting 模型，实现单步生成轨迹，并用「噪声向量与其相反数成对解码后平均」消除壳层偏差，在 NAVSIM 上取得 93.75 PDMS。
AI.relevance_reason: 论文不涉及视觉推理，但其把迭代采样压入训练、以一对反极样本平均抵消位移的单步生成思路，可能为 LVR 中并行或一步生成 latent 推理状态、以及采样误差抑制提供可供核查的方法线索。

title: When Does Exploration Prevent Collapse? Three Regimes and the Path of the Reward in Self-Consistency Training
summary: Test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL) adapts a model without labels by rewarding answers that agree with the majority, but it collapses the policy onto its majority answer and can remove the correct answer from the samples. Exploration can prevent this collapse, yet its strength is chosen by trial and error, and how the training algorithm changes the required strength is unclear. We model training on a single problem as a continuous flow of the logits of a softmax policy and analyze which policies are stable as the exploration coefficient varies. Only collapsed policies are stable below a lower boundary and only policies spread over many answers above an upper boundary, and we derive these boundaries in closed form for an agreement reward with smoothing toward the uniform policy, compute them for the majority reward of TTRL on policies with one leading answer and bound them with interval arithmetic for actions on ordered bins. We prove that under exact gradients, the learning rate and, in a mean-field model, the normalization of GRPO leave these boundaries unchanged when exploration passes through them together with the reward but shift them when exploration bypasses them. Exact sums on these policies then show that a bonus for rare answers needs a coefficient above $1/\log(G-1)$ for groups of $G$ samples before the normalization and about two to three times that after it. In free-form TTRL on MATH-500, a bonus placed before the normalization prevented collapse and kept more correct answers among the samples, although it lowered pass@1.

AI.brief_summary: 论文将单题上的自一致性训练（TTRL）建模为 softmax 策略 logits 的连续流，解析推导出探索系数使策略稳定于「坍缩」与「分散」两端的上下边界，并分析学习率与 GRPO 归一化对边界的影响，最后在 MATH-500 上用罕见答案奖励做验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 探索强度与策略坍缩的边界刻画可能为 latent 推理训练中的探索系数选取、奖励归一化和样本多样性消失提供可核查线索，但其对象是纯文本 TTRL，能否迁移到 latent 状态与视觉证据筛选尚不明确。

title: What Do LLM Judges Actually Verify? Matched Controls and Record Gaps for Document Currency
comment: 37 pages, 6 figures, including a 13-page supplementary case study. Code, data and all judge replies: https://github.com/unnatibshah/what-do-llm-judges-verify
summary: LLM judges often check, against an amendment record, whether the documents an answer cites are still in force. Such records are rarely complete. From a table of replacements, our test generates matched answers citing a replaced document, its successor, the replaced document before its replacement, and an older document that a newer one updated without replacing; it removes links from the record and scores each finding by its stated reason. On 48 replacements from the IETF RFC index, judges given a correct record caught nearly every replaced citation, as a lookup would. On the 24 faults whose link we removed, every judge caught more from the texts alone than with the record: Gemini 3.1 Pro 23/24 against 1/24, GPT-5.5 23/24 against 9/24, Claude Opus 4.5 17/24 against 9/24 and Gemma 4 26B 13/24 against 0/24. The drop recurred on a second draw of removed links. Most misses carried no finding; in an exploratory run with a conflict code, only Gemini used it often. Rewording the gap as "no replacement recorded" did not help; presenting the record as an unverified note, or warning that it was incomplete, restored most lost catches for Gemini, GPT-5.5 and Claude (significant after correction for the first two) but at most 5 of 13 for Gemma; where catches returned, so did false alarms on updates. With both texts, judges mostly told replacements from updates; every update flagged had a near-identical title. A descriptive case study on Indian rooftop-solar rules is appended; we release the harness.

AI.brief_summary: 论文用 IETF RFC 的替换表构造配对测试集，检验给定「文档替换记录」时 LLM 判官能否识别已失效引用，并人为删去记录中的链接，比较判官在有无记录、不同措辞与免责提示下的漏检与误报。

title: Alignment Flywheel-Guided Suppression Patching for Interactionless Inverse Reinforcement Learning
comment: Accepted for The 38th Benelux Conference on Artificial Intelligence and the 35th Belgian Dutch Conference on Machine Learning
summary: Learned reward models allow reinforcement-learning agents to use demonstrations, implicit feedback, safety constraints, social norms, or other sources that do not provide a complete hand-designed scalar reward. However, a learned reward model can assign high reward to unwanted behavior. A policy can exploit these errors during training. Later requirements can also identify additional regions where the deployed reward should change. We introduce \emph{flywheel-guided patching}, a mechanism for making such localized corrections without retraining the learned evaluator. An Alignment Flywheel identifies overgeneralized or constraint-violating regions and compiles verified findings into suppression patches. We instantiate the mechanism for Interactionless Inverse Reinforcement Learning using MoE-GUIDE, placing patches in the model's latent space and retrieving only a small local subset during online reward evaluation. In the main MuJoCo benchmark, we evaluate patching without expert-state reset warm starts. We also test whether operator-specified norms absent from the demonstrations can be compiled into the same reward interface and compare this with enforcing the corresponding rules online. The results show that localized corrective information can modify an existing learned reward without providing a complete replacement reward. Compilation can reuse judgments that are expensive or unavailable during control. Cheap deterministic rules may be simpler to check directly at each step. Code for MoE-GUIDE, Alignment Flywheel, and flywheel patching is at https://github.com/decide-ugent/Alignment-Flywheel.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 flywheel-guided patching：用 Alignment Flywheel 找出奖励模型过泛化或违反约束的区域，编译为抑制补丁放入 MoE-GUIDE 的 latent space，在线奖励评估时只检索少量局部补丁，从而在不重训评测器的情况下局部修正已学奖励，并在 MuJoCo 上与在线规则执行做比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「把局部修正信息编码进潜空间、按需检索小规模子集」的机制，可能为 LVR 中向 latent 推理状态注入外部证据或做局部编辑提供可核查的方法线索，但任务与多模态推理距离较远，需人工判断可迁移性。

title: The Verifier Is Part of the Simulator: Evidence-View Gaming in Agentic Equation Discovery
comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop "Sim2Science: ML with Imperfect Scientific Models". 28 pages, 5 figures. Code: https://github.com/oroikono/kagamaya
summary: A growing number of agentic pipelines search for governing equations: an agent proposes laws and a verifier checks them against simulated trajectories. The verifier sees only a numerical summary: integrals against test functions on a time grid. That summary carries its own discretization error, making the verifier part of the simulator. We freeze the trajectory, candidate library, verifier and thresholds, leaving the agent one move: which permitted summary to admit. Without scores or language models, finer time grids reduce numerical discrepancies and false library rejections. On PDEBench, the verifier instead accepts equations missing diffusion on score-selected summaries. Maximizing a public score rewarding decisive verdicts and larger mismatches when rejecting the library wrongly rejects all 1,500 in-library cases; retrospectively retuning score constants on a separate bank reduces errors to 13/180 at best. We call this evidence-view gaming: reward hacking by choice of permitted summary. In single-turn forced-choice tests, Claude models rarely choose summaries giving wrong verdicts when asked to be accurate, but often do so when asked to maximize the score or report missing physics. In separate trust prompts, they often rank those harmful summaries least trustworthy. Requiring several summaries to agree reduces errors but often withholds a verdict and performs worse than a fixed fine view on PDEBench: a safeguard, not a certificate. Evidence chosen after its verdict is known cannot alone authorize a claim.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究 agentic 方程发现中验证器只接收数值摘要（时间网格上测试函数积分）的问题，指出摘要自带离散化误差使验证器成为模拟器的一部分；在冻结轨迹、候选库与阈值的设定下，仅让 agent 选择提交哪份允许摘要，展示了「证据视图博弈」式 reward hacking，并测试 Claude 模型的选择倾向与多摘要一致性防护。
AI.relevance_reason: 将「呈现哪份证据」视为可被奖励指标钻空子的动作，与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、验证器与奖励设计、以及结论能否被授权的问题可能相通，多视图一致只是保障而非证书的结论可供核查。

title: Profile-aware diagnostics of discarded parameter-Hessian mass
summary: A discarded parameter-Hessian fraction depends on the diagonal profile and parameter partition; it is not the Fisher information discarded by K-FAC. We compare off-block squared Frobenius mass with group-size and measured diagonal-profile references at specified weights, inputs and coordinates. Similar initial fractions in ResNet-18 and its skip-free twin accompany different profiles. On the same saved trained ResNet-18 states, changing from stage groups to layers moves estimated mass from below to above the profile envelope. An approximate joint conditional Monte Carlo screen resolves this crossing in 6/6 seed/input cells; the skip-free network has 2 resolved and 4 unresolved comparisons. A separate comparison of nine saved states under two geometry draws splits the full model residual into off-group Hessian action and its remainder: gradient, within-group action and damping. At unit correction scale, off-group input alone increases loss in 17 of 18 state-geometry comparisons; in nine of those cases, the full candidate has lower loss than the remainder-only candidate. After correction-norm matching, seven of the ten comparisons that initially favoured full favour the remainder. These finite-loss contrasts depend on scale and do not establish a restoration benefit.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断分块近似下被丢弃的参数 Hessian 质量如何依赖对角 profile 与参数分组，在 ResNet-18 与其无跳连版本上比较 off-block 平方 Frobenius 质量与分组规模、实测对角参考，并用条件 Monte Carlo 与范数匹配的候选对比做核查。
